lines: Though this suffering Thou didst know,
Love would come to bear our woe.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: When we think of love like this,
Joy and shame our hearts possess;
Joy, that Thou couldst pity thus;
Shame, for such returns from us.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Yet we hope the day to see
When to Thee, in glory, brought,
We shall serve Thee as we ought.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Now, O Lord, we wait for Thee,
May we ever for Thee live,
Till Thy saints Thou dost receive.

hymns.title: It was alone the Savior prayed
hymns.author: Benjamin H. Price

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: It was alone the Savior stood
Alone the crown of thorns He wore,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: He gave Himself to save His own,
He suffered, bled and died alone, alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Alone upon the cross He hung
Forsaken then by God and man.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: He gave Himself to save His own,
He suffered, bled and died alone, alone.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Can you reject such matchless love?
Come, give your all in gratitude,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: He gave Himself to save His own,
He suffered, bled and died alone, alone.

hymns.title: O dearest Lord, what law hast Thou e’er broken
hymns.author: Jean de Fecamp (1000-1079); Adapted by Johann Heermann (1585-1647) bio; Translated by Catherine Winkworth
hymns.lyricist: Jean de Fecamp (1000-1079); Adapted by Johann Heermann (1585-1647) bio; Translated by Catherine Winkworth

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: They crown Thy head with thorns, they smite,
With cruel mockings to the cross they urge Thee;
They give Thee gall to drink, they still decry Thee;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: What punishment so strange is suffered yonder?
The shepherd dies for sheep that loved to wander;
The Master pays the debt His servants owe Him,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The sinless Son of God must die in sadness;
The sinful child of man may live in gladness;
Man forfeited his life and is acquitted—

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O mighty King, no time can dim Thy glory!
How shall I spread abroad Thy wondrous story?
How shall I find some worthy gift to proffer?

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: I’ll think upon Thy mercy without ceasing;
That earth’s vain joys no more to me be pleasing;
To do Thy will shall be my sole endeavor

hymns.title: Lord, we treasure with affection
hymns.author: M. W. Biggs; Chorus by Witness Lee (1905-1997)
hymns.lyricist: M. W. Biggs; Chorus by Witness Lee (1905-1997)

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Praise Thee, Savior! Praise Thee, Savior!
Give Thee glory for the [A]life we [D]gain!

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Deep Thy sorrow then, Lord Jesus,
Deeper far than thought can reach;
Far beyond all tongues to teach.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Praise Thee, Savior! Praise Thee, Savior!
Praise Thee, Lord, for sinners slain!
Give Thee glory! Give Thee glory!
Give Thee glory for the life we gain!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: None could follow there, blest Savior,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Praise Thee, Savior! Praise Thee, Savior!
Praise Thee, Lord, for sinners slain!
Give Thee glory! Give Thee glory!
Give Thee glory for the life we gain!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou didst measure then sin’s distance,
Darkness, wrath and curse were Thine;
Thus we learn Thy love divine!

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Praise Thee, Savior! Praise Thee, Savior!
Praise Thee, Lord, for sinners slain!
Give Thee glory! Give Thee glory!
Give Thee glory for the life we gain!

hymns.title: O Christ, what burdens bow’d Thy head
hymns.author: Anne Ross Cousin

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Death and the curse were in our cup,
But Thou hast drained the last dark drop—
That bitter cup—love drank it up;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O Christ, it fell on Thee!
Thou wast sore stricken of Thy God;
There’s not one stroke for me.
Thy tears, Thy blood, beneath it flowed;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The tempest’s awful voice was heard,
O Christ, it broke on Thee!
Thy open bosom was my ward,
It braved the storm for me.
Thy form was scarred, Thy visage marred;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Thy blood the flaming blade must slake;
Thy heart its sheath must be—
All for my sake, my peace to make;
Now sleeps that sword for me.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: For me, Lord Jesus, Thou hast died,
And I have died in Thee;
Thou’rt ris’n: my bands are all untied,
And now Thou liv’st in me.
When purified, made white, and tried,

hymns.title: O Head once full of bruises
hymns.author: Bernard of Clairvaux (1090-1153) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Which Thou didst pay in blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: When Thou for us didst bleed.
We see Thee face to face.

hymns.title: My song is love unknown
hymns.author: Samuel Crossman (1623-1683)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He came from His blest throne
But men made strange, and none

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: They rise and needs will have
The Prince of life they slay.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: In life, no house, no home
My Lord on earth might have;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Here might I stay and sing,

hymns.title: Thy sorrows, Savior, we retrace
hymns.author: F. Allaben

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: What love and grace illume Thy [C]face

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: What scorn and outrage Thee befell:
Deep shame and woe, rude blow on blow,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: But oh, what grief, what agony,
Burst over Thee on Calv’ry’s tree,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Creation’s Head is He who bled—

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: E’en now from saints, in concord sweet,
For, O, ’tis meet glad songs should greet

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: But when Thy glorious face we see,
How shall the bursting paean swell!
Our souls shall be outpoured for Thee—

hymns.title: Jesus! Source of life eternal
hymns.author: Ernest Christoph Homburg (1605-1681)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou, O Son of God! wert bearing
Thou, the King of glory, wearing,
For our sake, the crown of thorn:
From the chains of sin for ever;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All the shame men heaped upon Thee,
Not the pains of death too bitter,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Savior, thus to Thee we give:
For Thy death, whereby we live;
All the grief Thou wert enduring,
All the bliss Thou wert securing,

hymns.title: Tis midnight, and on Olive’s brow
hymns.author: William Bingham Tappan (1794-1849)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The Savior wrestles lone with fears—
E’en that disciple whom He loved
Heeds not his Master’s grief and tears.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Man of Sorrows weeps in blood;
Yet He that hath in anguish knelt
Is not forsaken by His God.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Is borne the song that angels know
Unheard by mortals are the strains
That sweetly soothe the Savior’s woe.

hymns.title: The Maker of the universe
hymns.author: Frederick William Pitt (1859-1943)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: His holy fingers made the bough
Which grew the thorns that crowned His brow.
The nails that pierced His hands were mined

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He made the forest whence there sprung
The tree on which His body hung.
He died upon a cross of wood,
Yet made the hill on which it stood.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The sky that darkened o’er His head
By Him above the earth was spread.
The sun that hid from Him its face
By His decree was poised in space.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: The spear which spilled His precious blood
Was tempered in the fires of God.
The grave in which His form was laid,
Was hewn in rocks His hands had made.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: The throne on which He now appears
But a new glory crowns His brow.
And every knee to Him shall bow.

hymns.title: When we survey the wondrous cross
hymns.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Our God forbid that we should boast,
Save in the death of Christ, our Lord;
All the vain things that charm us most,
We’d sacrifice them to His blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There from His head, His hands, His feet,
Sorrow and love flowed mingled down;
Did e’er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: His dying crimson, from His head
Spreads o’er His body on the tree;
To all the world then am I dead,
And all the world is dead to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Were the whole realm of nature ours,
That were an offering far too small;
Love that transcends our highest pow’rs,
Demands our heart, our life, our all.

hymns.title: We sing the praise of Him who died
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly (1769-1855)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Inscribed upon the Cross we see
In shining letters, God is love!
He bears our sins upon the tree,
He brings us mercy from above.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Cross: it takes our guilt away;
It holds the fainting spirit up;
It cheers with hope the gloomy day,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The balm of life, the cure of woe,
The measure and the pledge of love,
The angels’ theme in heav’n above.

hymns.title: Behold! behold the Lamb of God
hymns.author: Joseph Hoskins (1745-1788); Alfred P. Gibbs, v. 5
hymns.lyricist: Joseph Hoskins (1745-1788); Alfred P. Gibbs, v. 5

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: On the cross! On the cross!
Behold His bleeding hands and side,
On the cross! On the cross!
The sun withholds its rays of light,
The heav’ns are clothed in shades of night,
While Jesus wins the glorious fight,
On the cross! On the cross!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: By faith we see Him lifted up,
On the cross! On the cross!
He drinks for us the bitter cup,
On the cross! On the cross!
The rocks do rend, the mountains quake,
While Jesus all our sins doth take,
While Jesus suffers for our sake,
On the cross! On the cross!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: And now the mighty deed is done,
On the cross! On the cross!
The battle fought, the vict’ry won,
On the cross! On the cross!
To heav’n He turns triumphant eyes;
Then bows His sacred head and dies,
On the cross! On the cross!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: But now He’s ris’n, ascended, crowned,
On the throne! On the throne!
Heav’n’s highest place for Him is found,
On the throne! On the throne!
Our hearts we low in worship bow,
And join, as one, to hail Him now:
“Worthy, O Lamb of God, art Thou!”
On the throne! On the throne!

hymns.title: Alas! and did my Savior bleed
hymns.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Was it for sins that I had done

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Well might the sun in darkness hide,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thus might I hide my blushing face
And melt mine eyes to tears.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: But drops of grief can ne’er repay
The debt of love I owe;
Here Lord, I give myself away:

hymns.title: Himself He could not save
hymns.author: Albert Midlane (1825-1909)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Our sins’ full weight must fall
For nothing less can God accept
In payment of that fearful debt.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He bore the penalty of guilt
When on the cross His blood was spilt.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: There ne’er was love like His!
Such love should melt a heart of stone,
Till praise flows forth to Him alone!

hymns.title: No blood, no altar now
hymns.author: Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)
hymns.composer: From Hymns of Worship and Remembrance

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [A7]To [D]purge the soul from guilt, and [G]cleanse the [D]red[A7]dest [D]stains.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: We thank Thee for the blood,
The blood of Christ, God’s Son
The blood by which our peace is made,
Delivering us from hell, and sin, and woe;
That His eternal life God may to us bestow.

hymns.title: Not all the blood of beasts
hymns.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: My faith would lay her hand
On that dear head of Thine,
While like a penitent I stand,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My soul looks back to see
When hanging on the cursed tree,
And knows her guilt was there.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: We bless the Lamb with cheerful voice,

hymns.title: Man of Sorrows, what a name
hymns.author: Philip Paul Bliss (1838-1876)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In my place condemned He stood;
Sealed my pardon with His blood;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Spotless Lamb of God was He;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Lifted up was He to die,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: When He comes, our glorious King,
To His kingdom us to bring,
Then anew this song we’ll sing

hymns.title: The veil is rent! Lo! Jesus stands
hymns.author: James George Deck (1807-1884)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: His precious blood is sprinkled there,
And His own wounds in heav’n declare
His work on earth is done.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: ’Tis finished!” on the cross He said,
’Tis finished: now He lives to plead

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: ’Tis finished!” Here our souls can rest,
By Him, our Sacrifice and Priest

hymns.title: O solemn hour! O hour alone
hymns.author: James George Deck (1807-1884)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Of life and death the tree!
Which look with rapt, adoring eyes,
O cross of Christ, where all His pain
And death is our eternal gain.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O how our inmost hearts do move,
The death of the incarnate Love!
What shame, what grief, what joy we prove,
That He should die for us!
Our hearts were broken by that cry,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Worthy of death, O Lord, we were;
In grace Thou, spotless Lamb, didst bear
Thyself our sins, and guilt, and fear;
With Thee, our Surety, we have died;
With Thee, we there were crucified.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Quickened with Thee with life divine,
Raised with Thee from the dead;
Thine Own, now human and divine,
Shall with Thee in Thy glories shine,
We, who were worthy but to die,

hymns.title: Jesus, the sinner’s Friend
hymns.author: Mrs. Pennefather

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: We claim it as our own;
The Father must accept and bless

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Ours is the blessing, Thine the curse;
We live, for Thou hast died.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: No mortal voice can sing the song

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Thy face we all shall see,
Clothed in our blood-bought robes of white,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: And give ten thousand thanks to Thee,

hymns.title: How sweet is the story of Christ’s boundless love
hymns.author: R. D. Edwards

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]How sweet is the story of [A]Christ's boundless [D]love,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Sound His praise! Sound His praise!
Praise His name! Praise His name!
We give Him the glory, our [A]Savior and [D]Friend;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: How wondrous the story! the law’s holy claims
Were met by the blood which redemption proclaims.
The judgment of sin has been borne by the Son,
Who glorified God in the work He has done.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Sound His praise! Sound His praise!
All the work has been done;
Praise His name! Praise His name!
We give Him the glory, our Savior and Friend;
Our song is of Jesus and never will end.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: How brilliant the glory where Christ is enthroned
How rightly His name above others is owned!
Yes, Jesus, the Savior, the glory-crowned Lord,
Is worthy by all to be ever adored.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Sound His praise! Sound His praise!
All the work has been done;
Praise His name! Praise His name!
We give Him the glory, our Savior and Friend;
Our song is of Jesus and never will end.

hymns.title: How pleasant is the sound of praise
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly (1769-1855)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: For Him Who washed us in His blood,
Let us our sweetest songs prepare;
He sought us wandering far from God,
And now preserves us by His care.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: One string there is of sweetest tone,
Reserved for sinners saved by grace;
And touched by one peculiar race.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Though angels may with rapture see
How mercy flows in Jesus’ blood,
It is not theirs to prove, as we,
The cleansing virtue of this flood.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Though angels praise the heavenly King,
And worship Him as God alone,
“He wears our nature on the throne.”

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Lord, we adore Thy wondrous love,
Which brought Thee here to bleed and die
That Thou lost sinners may restore
And to the Father bring them nigh.

hymns.title: Hail, Thou once despised Jesus
hymns.author: John Bakewell (1721-1819)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: All our sins on Thee were laid;
All who trust Thee are forgiven
Through the virtue of Thy blood;
Opened are the things of heaven,
Grace shines forth to man from God.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Where for us Thou dost abide;
We, by faith, do now adore Thee,
There, for us Thou now art pleading,
There Thou dost our sorrows share,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Meet it is for us to give.
In that day Thy saints will meet Thee,
Joyful hearts will ever greet Thee,
Source of joy to all the throng!

hymns.title: Glory be to Jesus
hymns.author: Edward Caswall (1814-1878)

hymns.title: How wonderful redemption is
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Not seen, nor heard, nor [A]e'er conceived

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: For us Thou on the Cross wast pierced,
That life divine be giv’n to us,
Thy precious blood has made us clean,
We now are one with Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou art the grain divine that died
Which, blent and formed, Thy Body are.
We are the increase of Thyself,
Through us Thou livest and dost move

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Since we’re Thy Body, Thou may come
In us Thou may obtain Thy home
Thy heart to satisfy and please,
Now in one Body with Thyself,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: While in remembrance now we meet
For Thy redemption great and full
We’re filled with praise to Thee.
Since we are made Thy Body, Lord,
We would give thanks and worship Thee

hymns.title: Christ the Lord is ris’n indeed
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Where, O Death, is now thy sting?
Dying once He all doth save,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Fought the fight, the battle won,
Death in vain forbade Him rise,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Soar we now where Christ hath led,
Made like Him, like Him we rise,
Free from all the earthly ties,

hymns.title: Christ is risen! Hallelujah
hymns.author: John Samuel Bewley Monsell (1811-1875)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Christ is risen! All the sadness
Of His earthly life is o’er;
Through the open gates of gladness
He returns to life once more;
Death and hell before Him bending,
He doth rise the Victor now,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Christ is risen from the dead.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Death nor hell shall us enthrall;
We are Christ’s, in Him forever
Of our trembling hearts have ceased,
Let us rise and keep the feast.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Christ is risen from the dead.

hymns.title: Hallelujah, He is risen
hymns.author: Philip Paul Bliss (1838-1876)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Sends the witness of the Spirit
He is risen, He is risen,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Death for aye has lost his sting;
From the grave “His own” will bring:
He is risen, He is risen,

hymns.title: The Lord is ris’n; and death’s dark judgment flood
hymns.author: William Paton MacKay (1839-1885)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]The Lord is ris'n; and death's dark [D]judgment [G]flood
Is passed, in Him who [A]bought us [A7]with His [D]blood.
The [G]Lord is ris'n: we stand beyond the doom

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lord is ris’n: with Him we also rose,
And in His grave see vanquished all our foes.
The Lord is ris’n: beyond the judgment land,
In Him, in resurrection-life we stand.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Lord is ris’n: and now redeemed to God,
We tread the desert which His feet have trod.
The Lord is ris’n: the sanctu’ry’s our place,
Where now we dwell before the Father’s face.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The Lord is ris’n: the Lord is gone before.
We long to see Him, and to sin no more.
The Lord is ris’n: our triumph-shout shall be,
“Thou hast prevailed! Thy people, Lord, are free!”

hymns.title: Thine be the glory, risen, conqu’ring Son
hymns.author: Edmond Louis Budry (1854-1932); Translated by Richard B. Hoyle
hymns.lyricist: Edmond Louis Budry (1854-1932); Translated by Richard B. Hoyle

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Lo! Jesus meets us, risen from the tomb;
Lovingly He greets us, scatters fear and gloom;
Let the Church with gladness, hymns of triumph sing,
For her Lord now liveth, death hath lost its sting.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Thine be the glory, risen, conqu’ring Son,
Endless is the vict’ry Thou o’er death hast won.

hymns.title: Thou, Lord, to death’s domain
hymns.author: L. G. Milner

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: But Thou hast burst the grave,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Out of Thy death has sprung

hymns.title: Low in the grave He lay
hymns.author: Robert Lowry (1826-1899)

sections.label: Chorus
lines: And He [C]lives for[A]ever with His [D]saints to [D7]reign.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Up from the grave He arose,
With a mighty triumph o’er His foes
He arose a Victor from the dark domain,
And He lives forever with His saints to reign.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Up from the grave He arose,
With a mighty triumph o’er His foes
He arose a Victor from the dark domain,
And He lives forever with His saints to reign.

hymns.title: Praise Him! praise Him! Christ is Victor
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]Praise Him! praise Him! Christ is Victor!
Sin is judged, old Adam finished,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: God hath raised Him from the dead!
All the pow’r of death is swallowed,
Man from death to life is led!
Broken through are hell and darkness

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Praise Him! Christ hath now ascended!
God hath raised Him to the throne!
Far above all rule and power,
He the highest Name doth own!

hymns.title: Hallelujah! sing to Jesus
hymns.author: William Chatterton Dix (1837-1898)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Are we left in sorrow now;
Though the clouds from sight received Him
When the forty days were o’er,
Shall our hearts forget His promise,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou on earth our food, our stay;
Come to Thee from day to day.
On the throne of the Almighty

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: His the scepter, His the throne;
Hark, the songs of His redeemed ones
Hath redeemed us by His blood.

hymns.title: To Thee, dear Lord, O Christ of God
hymns.author: Anne Ross Cousin

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: To Thee, dear Lord, O Christ of God,
And robbed him of his sting.
The house of dust enthralls no more,
For Thou, the strong to save,
Thyself doth guard that silent door,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: To Thee, dear Lord, O Christ of God,
For Thou hast crushed beneath Thy rod
And plunged in Thine imperial strength
And brought Thy trophy up at length

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: To Thee, dear Lord, O Christ of God,
Thou hast redeemed us with Thy blood
God’s saving strength Thine arm upbore,
The arm that set us free;
Be to Thy God and Thee.

hymns.title: Hark! ten thousand voices crying
hymns.author: John Nelson Darby (1800-1882) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Loud and far each tongue partaking

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All the mind in heav’n is one.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Crowned with light and joy unfading,
Hail Him as the great “I AM.”

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Loudly swells the song of praise;

hymns.title: Far above all is our Savior enthroned
hymns.author: H. E. G.

sections.label: Chorus
lines: High as His members up[C]on Him we [B]call,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When the fierce tempest, uplifting its waves,
Seeks to engulf us, we cry and He saves;
Looking to Jesus, upheld by His hand,
Tread we the billows as safe as on land.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Far above all! Far above all!
Jesus the crucified far above all!
High as His members upon Him we call,
God hath exalted Him far above all!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: High are the cities that dare our assault,

Over the hills and the valleys,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: But for the showers we plead.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There shall be showers of blessing;
Send them upon us, O Lord!
Grant to us now a refreshing;
Come, and now honor Thy Word.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: But for the showers we plead.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: There shall be showers of blessing;
O that today they might fall,
Now as to God we’re confessing,
Now as on Jesus we call!

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: But for the showers we plead.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: There shall be showers of blessing,
If we but trust and obey;
If we let God have His way.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: But for the showers we plead.

hymns.title: Praise waiteth Thee in mercy’s court
hymns.author: Mary E. Maxwell

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Come, as the Spirit, Lord, today,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise for what Thou our God hast wrought;
The cloud on faith’s horizon seen,
Praise for Thine own right way, dear Lord,
But as Thy plans unfolded lie,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Room for the floods of blessing now,
E’en while we praise, the heavens rend,
In power come from on high;

hymns.title: Come, Lord, as the Spirit come
hymns.author: Charles William Fry (1838-1882)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: From the Father to the Son,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: On the altar now we lay
Soul and body, mind and will;

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Come, oh Lord, Great Spirit, come!
Let the mighty deed be done!
See us waiting for the fire,
See us waiting for the fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Though as dear as a right eye,
Who for us did bleed and die.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Come, oh Lord, Great Spirit, come!
Let the mighty deed be done!
See us waiting for the fire,
See us waiting for the fire.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Now, by faith, the gift I claim,
Bought for me by blood divine:

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Come, oh Lord, Great Spirit, come!
Let the mighty deed be done!
See us waiting for the fire,
See us waiting for the fire.

hymns.title: God sent His mighty pow’r
hymns.author: Delia T. White

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: My all from day to day.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: The fire of heav’nly love is
The fire of heav’nly love is

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: No good that I have done,
He saves me by His grace.
The fire is in my soul.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: The fire of heav’nly love is
The fire of heav’nly love is

hymns.title: Jesus, Thine all-victorious love
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, that in me the sacred fire
Burn up the dross of base desire,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He, who at Pentecost didst fall,
Thy Holy Ghost, for Him I call;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Refining fire, go through my heart,
Scatter Thy life through every part,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: My steadfast soul, from falling free,
While Christ is all the world to me,
And all my heart is love,
And all my heart is love.

hymns.title: Where the sprinkling of the blood is
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Bringing God to man for aye.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Blood doth speak of what God worketh,
Ointment, what He is for us;
By His work and by His person
God Himself is blent with us.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: By the blood of Christ’s redemption
We are cleansed from all alloy;
By th’ anointing of the Spirit

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: We with God are kept in one;
By the blood and by the ointment
God, our portion full, is won.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: We in faith must claim the cleansing
When we need the precious blood,
Thus to live and walk with God.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: God as light we’ll then be knowing,
And in God as life e’er growing,
God as power we will prove.

hymns.title: Divine anointing in me dwelleth
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: It ever [C]leads me in the [G]Lord to live

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: It is the moving of the Spirit
’Tis based upon the sprinkling of the blood,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: In my spirit the anointing dwells,
In my spirit the anointing dwells

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: With God’s own essence it anoints me,
That I may have His very element

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: In my spirit the anointing dwells,
In my spirit the anointing dwells

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In God, the light of truth, I’m walking,
And the love of grace I prove.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: In my spirit the anointing dwells,
In my spirit the anointing dwells

hymns.title: Fill me with Thy gracious Spirit
hymns.author: Elwood Haines Stokes (1815-1895)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou can’st fill me with Thy Spirit,
Though I cannot tell Thee how;
But I need Thee, greatly need Thee;
Come, dear Lord, and fill me now!

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Fill me now! Fill me now!
Fill me with Thy Spirit now!
Fill me with Thy Spirit now!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I am weakness, full of weakness;
At Thy sacred feet I bow;
Fill with strength, and fill me now!

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Fill me now! Fill me now!
Fill me with Thy Spirit now!
Fill me with Thy Spirit now!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Cleanse and comfort, bless and save me;

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Fill me now! Fill me now!
Fill me with Thy Spirit now!
Fill me with Thy Spirit now!

hymns.title: How I praise Thee, precious Savior
hymns.author: Mary E. Maxwell

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Just a channel, full of blessing,
To tell out Thy full salvation,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: But with all Thy wondrous grace,
Flowing through us, Thou canst use us

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Emptied that Thou shouldest fill me,
A clean vessel in Thine hand;
With no strength but as Thou givest

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: But with all Thy wondrous grace,
Flowing through us, Thou canst use us

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Witnessing Thy grace to save me,
Setting free from self and sin;
Thou hast bought me to possess me,
In Thy fulness, Lord, come in.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: But with all Thy wondrous grace,
Flowing through us, Thou canst use us

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O Lord, fill now with Thy Spirit
That the streams of living water
From our inner man may flow.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: But with all Thy wondrous grace,
Flowing through us, Thou canst use us

hymns.title: O Lord, with Thy Holy Ghost
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber, adapted (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O Lord, with Thy Holy Ghost,
Be it unto me, O Lord,
Let the life of Jesus be,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O Lord, with Thy Holy Ghost,
Cleansed and holy, pure and clean,
Let the life of Christ be seen;
Hold o’er me Thy gracious sway,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O Lord, with Thy Holy Ghost,
For Thy love, Thy light, Thy grace,
Just a channel all my days;
Till my Savior’s face I see,
Fill me, Lord, fill even me.

hymns.title: Lord, in Thy Spirit, take and fill my heart
hymns.author: George Croly (1780-1860)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I ask no dream, no prophet ecstasies,
No sudden rending of the veil of clay,
No angel visitant, no opening skies;
But take the dimness of my soul away.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Hast Thou not bid us love Thee, God and King?
All, all Thine own—soul, heart and strength and mind.
I see Thy cross—there teach my heart to cling.
Oh, let me seek Thee, and, oh, let me find.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Teach me to feel that Thou art always nigh;
Teach me the struggles of the soul to bear,
To check the rising doubt, the rebel sigh;
Teach me the patience of unanswered prayer.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Teach me to love Thee with a virgin love,
One holy passion filling all my frame;
Thus all the riches of Thyself to prove,
My heart an altar, and Thy love the flame.

hymns.title: Christ indeed was born of Spirit
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: All were Spirit born and filled,
As on them Christ breathed and willed.
Yet they still received the baptism
Of the Spirit from on high
When they were equipped for service,
And were clothed with pow’r thereby.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet they still received the baptism
Of the Spirit from on high
When some laid their hands upon them,
And were clothed with pow’r thereby.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: We are also born of Spirit
On the day when we believe,
And of Him we now are drinking
Yet we also must be baptized
With the Spirit from on high,
Thus to be equipped for service,
And be clothed with pow’r thereby.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Lord, baptize us with Thy Spirit!
This is what we need today;
Clothe us with Thy heav’nly power,
Bring us under its full sway.
Oh, baptize us in this hour!
This is all our earnest cry;
Now on us repeat Thine answer,
Clothe with power from on high.

hymns.title: Lord, we come to Thee, and with liberty
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, we look to Thee and with certainty
Claim we now from Thee show’r divine.
For Thy Body’s sake, may we show’r partake,
Thus be fitted for the work of Thine.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Shower! shower! pour on us Thy shower!
Pour Thy heav’nly shower from on high!
Shower! shower! pour on us Thy shower!
Boldly, as Thy Body, now we cry!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, we wait on Thee, and with surety
Claim we now from Thee fire divine.
For Thy gospel’s sake, may we fire partake,
That the People’s heart Thou may refine.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Fire! fire! give us tongues of fire!
To proclaim Thy message from on high!
Fire! fire! give us tongues of fire!
Boldly, as Thy Body, now we cry!

hymns.title: O Lord, we seek the power we need
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Chorus
lines: We are waiting, [A7]and to Thee we bow,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, come and visit us at this place,
Grant to Thy Church the gifts of Thy grace,
Fully with might our service embrace,
Clothe us with pow’r we pray!

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: We are waiting, and to Thee we bow,
In Thy presence all our need avow;
Give us Thy power, give even now,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Send us Thy power with its full sway,
As Thou didst send on Pentecost day;
Answer our prayer and make no delay,
Clothe us with pow’r we pray!

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: We are waiting, and to Thee we bow,
In Thy presence all our need avow;
Give us Thy power, give even now,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Here, as Thy Body, Thy pow’r we claim;
Claiming by faith in Thy mighty Name,
Thy heav’nly show’r with Thy heav’nly flame;
Clothe us with pow’r we pray!

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: We are waiting, and to Thee we bow,
In Thy presence all our need avow;
Give us Thy power, give even now,

hymns.title: Thy Holy Spirit, Lord, alone
hymns.author: Adapted from Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915) bio
hymns.lyricist: Adapted from Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: His power alone can turn our heart

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Thy Spirit of pow’r with might,
Send in our midst, we pray,
And come upon each seeking soul;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy Holy Spirit, Lord, can give
The gifts we seek to share;
His pow’r can signs and wonders work

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Thy Spirit of pow’r with might,
Send in our midst, we pray,
And come upon each seeking soul;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy Holy Spirit, Lord, can bring
The show’r we need this hour;
And while we seek, Lord Jesus, come

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Thy Spirit of pow’r with might,
Send in our midst, we pray,
And come upon each seeking soul;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Thy Spirit of pow’r with might,
Send in our midst, we pray,
And like a rushing, mighty wind

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Thy Spirit of pow’r with might,
Send in our midst, we pray,
And come upon each seeking soul;

hymns.title: What a blessed fact! What a tiding glad
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]In the Spirit we have been bap[D7]tized;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In the testament it is clearly told,
In the Spirit we have been baptized;
It is so complete, we need only hold,
In the Spirit we have been baptized.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Hold now this fact by living faith;
Hold now this accomplished fact by faith.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ upon the Church hath His Spirit poured,
In the Spirit we have been-baptized;
Share her portion now, share in full accord,
In the Spirit we have been baptized.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Share now this fact by living faith;
Share now this accomplished fact by faith.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: With the Body right, on the Body ground,
Move and act on this accomplished fact;
Sins and doubts condemn, wait no more around,
But by living faith now move and act.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Act on this fact by living faith;
Act on this accomplished fact by faith.

hymns.title: Christ the Savior hath ascended
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Crowned with glory and with honor
He hath made Him [G]Head of all things,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: From this Christ to God ascended
Poured upon the Church, His Body,
Thus the Lord of all in heaven
Thru His Church will be adored.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Into man He God hath brought;
Into God He man hath brought;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: He is seated on the throne;
All the lordship, all the headship,
And by pouring out His Spirit,
He as such might be made known.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: ’Tis by this, that in His Spirit
All the Church He hath baptized;
Thus the baptism of the Spirit

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Praise Him, He hath sent the Spirit

hymns.title: The Spirit of life is within us today
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]The Spirit of life is with[D]in us [D7]to[G]day,
Of [G]Him we may drink and be [C]filled thus with [D]Him,
Un[G]til as a river He [D]flows from [D7]with[G]in.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The Spirit of pow’r comes upon us today,
Who’s likened to clothing ourselves to array;
In Him we are baptized, with Him we are dressed,
For service equipping with power possessed.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Spirit of life is as breath glorious,
As spirit of life it is breathed into us;
The Spirit of pow’r doth the wind typify,
Which bloweth upon us with pow’r from on high.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Into His disciples the risen Lord breathed,
The Spirit of life thus to them He bequeathed;
Th’ ascended Lord poured at the Pentecost hour
Upon His disciples the Spirit of pow’r.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: The Spirit of life is within as the life,
The Spirit of power is giv’n for this life;
As blowing of wind brings the fresh air to breathe,
The Spirit of power to life doth bequeath.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: These are not two spirits apart and afar,
But of the one Spirit the two functions are,
To clothe us with God and to fill us within,
That we may be thoroughly mingled with Him.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Lord, fill with Thy Spirit of life every part,
That we may grow up in Thy life as Thou art;
And clothe us without with Thy Spirit of pow’r
Thy will to fulfill in Thy service each hour.

hymns.title: Through the Cross, O Lord, I pray
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]First the blood, and then the ointment,
If we pass not thru Golgotha,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Christ, the Rock, must first be smitten,
Ne’er could dwell in man below.
If with Christ we die completely,
Willing thus our all to lose,
He will clothe us with His power
And to win the world will use.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Through the Cross, O Lord, I pray,
Make me any price to pay,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: First the altar, then the fire,
If no loss, there’ll be no gain;
If our all has not been offered,
To the throne we’ll ne’er attain.
He to us will be committed
And thru us His pow’r display.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Through the Cross, O Lord, I pray,
Make me any price to pay,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: First we must prepare the vessels
That the Oil they may contain;
Dig the valley full of ditches
That they may be filled with Rain.
First we must go thru the Jordan
First in death we must be baptized,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Through the Cross, O Lord, I pray,
Make me any price to pay,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: When we see the ripened harvest
We may know that many seeds have
Fallen to the earth and died.
Ere the fruit of life may blossom,
If with Christ we’ve not been buried,
We’ll not feel the Spirit’s breath.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Through the Cross, O Lord, I pray,
Make me any price to pay,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Since it must be thus, I pray, Lord,
Help me go the narrow way;
Deal with pride and make me willing
I for greater power pray not,
Deeper death is what I need;
All the meaning of the Cross, Lord,
Work in me—for this I plead.

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: Through the Cross, O Lord, I pray,
Make me any price to pay,

hymns.title: Oh, from myself deliver
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, Lord, how dry my heart is,
It yearns and pants for Thee;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: How cold my heart has been, Lord,
So fill me with Thy Spirit,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh, may Thy Cross within me
Oh, may Thy Spirit fill me
On me and thru me pour.

hymns.title: Lord, the Spirit, Truth divine
hymns.author: Samuel Longfellow (1819-1892)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Glow within this heart of mine,
Perish self in Thy pure fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Fill and nerve this will of mine;
By Thee may I strongly live,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Still this restless heart of mine,
Speak to calm this tossing sea,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Gladden Thou this heart of mine;
In the desert ways I’ll sing:

hymns.title: Lord of light, with light divine
hymns.author: Andrew Reed (1787-1862)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord of power, with power divine,
Cleanse this guilty heart of mine;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord of joy, with joy divine,
Cheer this saddened heart of mine;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Dwell within this heart of mine;

hymns.title: Lord, Thou knowest all the hunger
hymns.author: F. H. Allen

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: How my soul hath [G]long been crav[D]ing

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Failure in my walk and witness,
Failure in my work I see;
Calling forth no praise to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Now to Thee my soul confesses
All its failure, all its sin;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Save me from myself, my Father,
From each subtle form of pride;
Lead me now with Christ to Calvary,
Show me I with Him have died.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: No more let it be my working,
Nor my wisdom, love, or power,
But the life of Jesus only,
Passing through me hour by hour.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Let the fulness of Thy Spirit
That the witness borne to others.
May bring glory, Lord, to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Father, in Thy Son’s Name pleading.
I believe my prayer is heard;
And I praise Thee for the answer.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Thou hast answered, Lord, I know.

hymns.title: Loved with everlasting love
hymns.author: George Wade Robinson (1838-1877)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Led by grace that love to [A]know;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Since I know, as now I know,
I am His, and He is mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Things that once were wild alarms
Doubt and care and self resign,
While He whispers in my ear,
I am His, and He is mine.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Who the Lord and me shall part?
Ah, with what a rest of bliss
Christ can fill the loving heart.
Heaven and earth may fade and flee,
But, while God and I shall be,
I am His, and He is mine.

hymns.title: Come and rejoice with me
hymns.author: Elizabeth Rundle Charles (1828-1896)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I, once so sick at heart,
Have met with One who knows my case,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And I have found a mighty arm

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My feet so wide did roam,
And One has brought me from afar,
To find in Him my home.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: For I have found a Friend
Who knows my heart’s most secret depths,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: I knew not of His love;
And He had loved so long,
With love so faithful and so deep,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: And now I know it all,
Have heard and known His voice,
And hear it still from day to day.

hymns.title: Of Jesus’ love that sought me
hymns.author: Lelia Naylor Morris (1862-1929)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: And caused the blind to see;
And still His great heart yearneth

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Sweeter as the years go by,
Sweeter as the years go by;
Sweeter as the years go by.

hymns.title: Jesus, Jesus, Jesus
hymns.author: A. Paget Wilkes

hymns.title: I’ve found a Friend, oh, such a Friend
hymns.author: James Grindlay Small (1817-1888)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]I've found a Friend, oh, [A]such a Friend!
He [D7]drew me with the [G]cords of love,
For [D]I am His, and [G]He is mine,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I’ve found a Friend, oh, such a Friend!
He bled, He died to save me;
And not alone the gift of life,
But His own self He gave me.
Naught that I have my own I call,
I hold it for the Giver;
My heart, my strength, my life, my all,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I’ve found a Friend, oh, such a Friend!
So kind, and true, and tender,
So wise a Counsellor and Guide,
From Him who loves me now so well,
What power my soul can sever?
Shall life or death, or earth or hell?

hymns.title: I stand all amazed at the love Jesus offers me
hymns.author: Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856-1932)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Confused at the grace that so [D7]fully He [G]proffers me;
That [A]for me, a sinner, He [A7]suffered, [A]He [D]bled and died.

sections.label: Chorus
lines: [G]O it [D]is [G]wonderful that He should [D]care for me

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I marvel that He would descend from His throne divine
To rescue a soul so rebellious and proud as mine;
That He should extend His great love unto such as I,
Sufficient to own, to redeem, and to justify.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: O it is wonderful that He should care for me
O it is wonderful, wonderful to me!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I think of His side, pierced and bleeding to pay the debt,
Such mercy, such love and devotion can I forget?
No, no! I will praise and adore at the mercy seat,
And testify all my desires He doth fully meet.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: O it is wonderful that He should care for me
O it is wonderful, wonderful to me!

hymns.title: I stand amazed in the presence
hymns.author: Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856-1932)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: For me it was in the garden,
He prayed: “Not my will, but Thine.”
He had no tears for His own griefs,
But sweat-drops of blood for mine.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: And my song shall ever be:
Is my Savior’s love for me!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And came from the world of light
To strengthen Him in the sorrows
He bore for my soul that night.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: And my song shall ever be:
Is my Savior’s love for me!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: He took my sins and my sorrows,
He made them His very own;
He bore the burden to Calv’ry,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: And my song shall ever be:
Is my Savior’s love for me!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: When with the ransomed in glory
His face I at last shall see,
’Twill be my joy through the ages
To sing of His love for me.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: And my song shall ever be:
Is my Savior’s love for me!

hymns.title: I am so glad that our Father in heav’n
hymns.author: Philip Paul Bliss (1838-1876)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [Am]Tells of His love in the [D7]Book He has [G]giv'n;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Though I forget Him and wander away,

There my burdened soul found liberty,

hymns.title: There is sunshine in my soul today
hymns.author: Eliza Edmunds Hewitt (1851-1920)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: There is music in my soul today,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: While the peaceful, happy moments roll;
When Jesus shows His smiling face
There is sunshine in my soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There is springtime in my soul today,
For when the Lord is near
The dove of peace sings in my heart,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: While the peaceful, happy moments roll;
When Jesus shows His smiling face
There is sunshine in my soul.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: There is gladness in my soul today,
And hope, and praise, and love,
For blessings which He gives me now,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: While the peaceful, happy moments roll;
When Jesus shows His smiling face
There is sunshine in my soul.

hymns.title: Grace there is my every debt to pay
hymns.author: Herbert Howard Booth (1862-1926)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Grace there is my every [A]debt to pay,
Pow'r to [G]keep me spotless [D]day by day,

hymns.title: I wandered in the shades of night
hymns.author: Judson W. Van de Venter (1855-1939)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]I wandered in the shades of night,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Since the Savior found me, [A]took away my [A7]sin,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Though clouds may gather in the sky,
However dark the world may be,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Sunlight, sunlight, in my soul today,
Sunlight, sunlight, all along the way,
Since the Savior found me, took away my sin,
I have had the sunlight of His love within.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: While walking in the light of God,
I press with holy vigor on

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Sunlight, sunlight, in my soul today,
Sunlight, sunlight, all along the way,
Since the Savior found me, took away my sin,
I have had the sunlight of His love within.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Soon I shall see Him as He is,
The Light that came to me;
Behold the brightness of His face,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Sunlight, sunlight, in my soul today,
Sunlight, sunlight, all along the way,
Since the Savior found me, took away my sin,
I have had the sunlight of His love within.

hymns.title: I am not skilled to understand
hymns.author: Dora Greenwell (1821-1882)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: What [A7]God hath willed, what [D]God hath planned;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I take Him at His word indeed:
For in my heart I find a need
Of Him to be my Savior!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: That He should leave His place on high
And come for sinful man to die,
You count it strange? So once did I

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: And, oh, that He fulfilled may see
The travail of His soul in me,
And with His work contented be,
As I with my dear Savior!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Yes, living, dying, let me bring
My strength, my solace from this spring—
That He who lives to be my King
Once died to be my Savior!

hymns.title: O happy day that fixed my choice
hymns.author: Philip Doddridge (1702-1751)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I am my Lord’s, and He is mine;
He drew me and I followed on,
Rejoiced to own the call divine.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: When Jesus washed my sins away!
He taught me how to watch and pray,
When Jesus washed my sins away!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Fixed on this blissful center, rest;
Here have I found a nobler part,
Here heav’nly pleasures fill my breast.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: When Jesus washed my sins away!
He taught me how to watch and pray,
When Jesus washed my sins away!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: High heav’n that hears the solemn vow,
That vow renewed shall daily hear!
Till in life’s latest hour I bow,
And bless, in death, a bond so dear.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: When Jesus washed my sins away!
He taught me how to watch and pray,
When Jesus washed my sins away!

hymns.title: Since Christ my soul from sin set free
hymns.author: Charles J. Butler (1860-)

sections.label: Chorus
lines: For it is Christ that [A7]I en[D]joy!

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The earth was once a bitter place
Till Jesus showed His smiling face;
Now joy’s begun within my soul,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: For it is Christ that I enjoy!
On land or sea, what matters where?
Where Jesus is, my joy is there.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: What matters where on earth we dwell?
On mountain top, or in the dell,
In cottage, or a mansion fair,
Where Jesus is, my joy is there.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: For it is Christ that I enjoy!
On land or sea, what matters where?
Where Jesus is, my joy is there.

hymns.title: As pants the hart for cooling streams
hymns.author: N. Tate (1652-1715); N. Brady (1639-1726)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Why restless, why cast down, my soul?
His aid for thee, and change these sighs

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: For Thee, my God, the living God,
Oh, when shall I behold Thy face,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: God of my strength, how long shall I,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Why restless, why cast down, my soul?
Hope still, and thou shalt sing
The praise of Him who is thy God,

hymns.title: My goal is God Himself, not joy, nor peace
hymns.author: Frances Brook

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: ’Tis His to lead me there— not [A7]mine, but [D]His—

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: So faith bounds forward to its goal in God,
And love can trust her Lord to lead her there;
Upheld by Him, my soul is following hard
Till God hath full fulfilled my deepest prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: No matter if the way be sometimes dark,
No matter though the cost be oft-times great,
He knoweth how I best shall reach the mark,
The way that leads to Him must needs be strait.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: One thing I know, I cannot say Him nay;
One thing I do, I press towards my Lord;
My God my glory here, from day to day,
And in the glory there my great Reward.

hymns.title: God the Almighty, Uncreated Life
hymns.author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: List to my [D]cry as [D7]I lie in the [G]dust,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, by the Cross, the passion of Thy Christ,
Oh, by the death of my Lord crucified,
From pow’r of darkness translate me today
Into the kingdom of Thy light to abide.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Fill from the center with Thine utmost filling,
Fill to circumf’rence, fill right to the brim;
Blaze forth, the light, the glory of Thy being
About and ’round me to the uttermost rim.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Life Uncreated, Thou most holy God,
Life-giving Spirit, oh, create in me
Something that speaks of Thee and of Thy glory,
Something compelling that will draw to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Father, I thank Thee that my quest is ended.
I reign in life with Christ upon the throne
How satisfied to triumph now in Him,
The Cross the touchstone that makes me His own.

hymns.title: In the wilderness for God
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Just a common bush to be,
Something in which God can dwell,
Something thru which God can speak,
Something thru which God can tell,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Flaming with no light of earth,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Nothing seen but just the flame;
Make me that, just that, O God,
For the glory of Thy Name.

hymns.title: I need Jesus, my need I now confess
hymns.author: George Orlia Webster (1866-1942)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: No [G]friend like [D]Him in times of deep dis[A]tress;
Though some may bear their [D]load alone,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Need Him when the storm- clouds [D7]low'r;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I need Jesus, I need a friend like Him,
A friend to guide when paths of life are dim;
I need Jesus, when foes my soul assail;
Alone I know I can but fail,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: I need Jesus, I need Jesus,
Need Him in the sunshine hour,
Need Him when the storm-clouds low’r;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I need Jesus, I need Him to the end;
No one like Him, He is the sinner’s friend;
I need Jesus, no other friend will do;
So constant, kind, so strong and true,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: I need Jesus, I need Jesus,
Need Him in the sunshine hour,
Need Him when the storm-clouds low’r;

hymns.title: Come in, O come! the door stands open now
hymns.author: Handley Carr Glyn Moule (1841-1920)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: The sun has [D7]set long [D]since the storms be[D7]gin;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Alas, ill-ordered shows the dreary room;
The household stuff lies heaped amidst the gloom,
The table empty stands, the couch undressed;
Ah, what a welcome for th’ Eternal Guest!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet welcome, and tonight; this doleful scene
Is e’en itself my cause to hail Thee in;
This dark confusion e’en at once demands
Thine own bright presence, Lord, and ord’ring hands.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I seek no more to alter things, or mend,
Before the coming of so great a Friend;
All were at best unseemly; and ’twere ill
Beyond all else to keep Thee waiting still.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Come, not to find, but make this troubled heart
A dwelling worthy of Thee as Thou art;
To chase the gloom, the terror, and the sin:
Come, all Thyself, yea come, Lord Jesus, in!

hymns.title: O blessed, living Lord
hymns.author: George West Frazer (1840-1896)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: To cleave to Thy blest side!
To gaze upon Thee where Thou art,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And more to Thine own stature grow,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The goal to which our hearts aspire—
To meet Thee in the air!

hymns.title: Thou Magnet of my soul
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]The life of self pul[G]sates no more,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: And let Thy garden yield to Thee

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The spoil that Thou hast won.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou Lord of Life and Light!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Straight from God’s heart of love;
I break my heart to give Thee room

hymns.title: Come, Jesus, Lord, with holy fire
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Let nothing now my heart divide,
Since with Thee I am crucified,
And live to God in Thee.
Dead to the world and all its toys,
Its idle pomp and fading joys,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Now with a quenchless thirst inspire,
Less than Thyself, oh, do not give,
In might Thyself within me live;
Come, all Thou hast and art.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My will be swallowed up in Thee,
Light in Thy light still may I see
Called the full strength of trust to prove,
Let all my quickened heart be love,

hymns.title: Love Divine, all love excelling
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Breathe, O breathe Thy loving Spirit
Let us all in Thee inherit,
Let us find the promised rest.
Take away the love of sinning;
End of faith, as its beginning,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Let us all Thy life receive;
May Thy presence e’er be with us,
Thee we would be always blessing,
Serve Thee as Thou wouldst approve,
Pray, and praise Thee without ceasing,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Pure and spotless let us be;
Let us see Thy great salvation
Till with Thee we take our place,
Till we cast our crowns before Thee,
Lost in wonder, love and praise.

hymns.title: O Light of light, shine in

End Thou this grief of sin,
O Joy of joys, come in!

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: To my poor heart come in!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O Life of life, pour in!
O Life of life, pour in!

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: To my poor heart come in!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O Love of love, flow in!
O Love of love, flow in!

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: To my poor heart come in!

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: To my poor heart come in!

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: My God and Lord, O come!
Of joys the Joy and Sum,
Make in this heart Thy home:
My God and Lord, O come!

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: To my poor heart come in!

hymns.title: O Everlasting Light
hymns.author: Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Sure guide of erring age or youth,
Lead me, and teach me too.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Bring me, in spite of foes, at length
To joy and light of day.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Pour down Thy fulness from above,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Lift off life’s load of care;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Thou art in heaven our all,
Our all on earth art Thou;
Upon Thy glorious Name we call,

hymns.title: O Love divine, by Christ revealed
hymns.author: Wilson Thomas Hogue (1852-1920)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O Light divine, by Christ displayed,
Source of all light, who flesh became,
Shed Thy bright beams upon my head,
Burn in my heart a constant flame.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O Truth divine, by Christ made known,
All truth must Thy reflection be;
Within my heart set up Thy throne,
And in Thy freedom make me free.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O Cross divine, by Christ endured,
Thou cross on which He groaned and died,
In Thy blest shadow let me hide.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O Peace divine, by Christ bestowed,
Thy heavenly dove to earth come down,
May He within make His abode,
My life with His dear presence crown.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: O Joy divine, by Christ possessed,
For which He did the cross endure,
Fill with Thyself and make me blest,

hymns.title: He died for me that I might live
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He died for me that I might die
O death so deep! O life so high!

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: O Jesus, my Lord and Savior,
Help me to fully follow Thee
In life and death and loving service,
As Thou hast lived and died for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He lives for me that I may live
Savior, to me Thy nature give,
And live Thy life in me.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: O Jesus, my Lord and Savior,
Help me to fully follow Thee
In life and death and loving service,
As Thou hast lived and died for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: He lives for me that I may give
His love to hearts that pine;
Let me like Him for others live,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: O Jesus, my Lord and Savior,
Help me to fully follow Thee
In life and death and loving service,
As Thou hast lived and died for me.

hymns.title: Lord, I would have Thyself in all Thy beauty
hymns.author: Mrs. J. I. McClelland

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [Em]Take Thou con[A7]trol of [A]all my life just [D]now;
In [A7]Thee to [D]live, and move, and [D7]have my [G]being,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Thy [G]blood was [D]shed to cleanse from sin, Lord [Em]Jesus,
I [G]take my [D]stand upon Thy word of [G]promise:

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Show me the things of which I am unconscious,
Lord, put Thy finger now upon my heart;
Whisper to me, through Thy blest Holy Spirit,
Tell me what grieves Him, that it may depart.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Thy blood was shed to cleanse from sin, Lord Jesus,
Thy risen life transforms the old to new;
I take my stand upon Thy word of promise:
Sin shall not have dominion over you!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou art my Victor over keen temptation,
Thou art my Shield, to meet the darts of sin;
Lord Jesus, Thou alone can keep me trusting,
And living out Thy glorious life within.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Thy blood was shed to cleanse from sin, Lord Jesus,
Thy risen life transforms the old to new;
I take my stand upon Thy word of promise:
Sin shall not have dominion over you!

hymns.title: Jesus, my life, Thyself apply
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Conqu’ror of hell and earth and sin,
Enter my soul and work within,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: More of Thy life, and more I have,
Bury me, Savior, in Thy grave,
That I with Thee may rise.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Reign in me, Lord; Thy foes control,
Who would not own Thy sway;
Diffuse Thine image through my soul;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Scatter the last remains of sin,
O make me glorious all within,

hymns.title: Jesus, Thy life is mine
hymns.author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1836-1879)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy life in me be shown,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy love, Thy joy, Thy peace,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Now at Thy word I claim,

hymns.title: Christ, whose glory fills the skies
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Dark and cheerless is the morn
Till Thy mercy’s beams I see,
Glad my eyes, and warm my heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Visit then this soul of mine,
Pierce the gloom of sin and grief;

hymns.title: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ
hymns.author: J. Temperley Grey

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
Beneath Thy Cross I die to self,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
So shall I think as Thou dost think,
And will as Thou dost will.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
And through this veil of mortal flesh,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
To be Thy slave, to do Thy will,

hymns.title: More love to Thee, O Lord
hymns.author: Elizabeth Prentiss

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: This all my prayer shall be:
More love, O Lord, to Thee,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: When they can sing with me,
More love, O Lord, to Thee,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: This still its prayer shall be:
More love, O Lord, to Thee,

hymns.title: Let me love Thee, Thou art claiming
hymns.author: Herbert Howard Booth (1862-1926)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Let that love in pow'r pre[A]vailing,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Let me love Thee, come revealing
All Thy love has done for me;
Let me see Thy love despising
All the shame my sins had brought;
What a price my pardon bought.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Let me love Thee, I am gladdest
When I’m loving Thee, the best;
For in sunshine or in sadness
I can find in Thee a rest;
But without Thee life is fading,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Let me love Thee, love is mighty,
Swaying realms of deed and thought;
By it I shall walk uprightly,
I shall serve Thee as I ought:
Love will triumph, love will dare.

hymns.title: Abide with me! fast falls the eventide
hymns.author: Henry Francis Lyte (1793-1847)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings:
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, thus abide with me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I need Thy presence every passing hour:
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, oh, abide with me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness:
Where is death’s sting? where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

hymns.title: I need Thee every hour
hymns.author: Annie Sherwood Hawks (1836-1918); Chorus by Robert Lowry (1826-1899)
hymns.lyricist: Annie Sherwood Hawks (1836-1918); Chorus by Robert Lowry (1826-1899)

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: I need Thee, oh, I need Thee;
Oh, bless me now, my Savior!

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: I need Thee, oh, I need Thee;
Oh, bless me now, my Savior!

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: I need Thee, oh, I need Thee;

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: I need Thee, oh, I need Thee;

hymns.title: Nothing between my soul and the Savior

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Keep the way clear! Let [A7]nothing bet[D]ween.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Habits of life, though harmless they seem,
Must not my heart from Him e’er sever;
He is my all, there’s nothing between.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Nothing between my soul and the Savior,
So that His blessed face may be seen;
Nothing preventing the least of His favor,
Keep the way clear! Let nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Nothing between, like pride or station;
Self-life or friends shall not intervene;
Though it may cost me much tribulation,
I am resolved; there’s nothing between.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Nothing between my soul and the Savior,
So that His blessed face may be seen;
Nothing preventing the least of His favor,
Keep the way clear! Let nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Nothing between, e’en many hard trials,
Though the whole world against me convene;
Watching with prayer and much self-denial,
I’ll triumph at last, with nothing between.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Nothing between my soul and the Savior,
So that His blessed face may be seen;
Nothing preventing the least of His favor,
Keep the way clear! Let nothing between.

hymns.title: Nothing between, Lord, nothing between
hymns.author: Evan H. Hopkins

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Let not earth’s din and noise
In it let me rejoice—Nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: No robe that self may wear—Nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Fading when Thou art near—Nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O’er my whole heart bear sway—Nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Thus may I walk with Thee,
Thine only let me be—Nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Bursts on my open sight—Nothing between.

hymns.title: Sun of my soul, Thou Savior dear
hymns.author: John Keble (1792-1866)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When the soft dews of kindly sleep
Be my last thought how sweet to rest

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Abide with me from morn till eve,
For without Thee I cannot live;
Abide with me when night is nigh,
For without Thee I dare not die.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Come near, and bless us when we wake,
Ere through the world our way we take;
Till in the ocean of Thy love
We lose ourselves in Thee above.

hymns.title: There is a place of quiet rest

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: A place where sin can[Dm]not molest,

sections.label: Verse 2

Near to the heart of God,
A place where we our Savior meet,
Near to the heart of God.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Sent from the heart of God,
Hold us, who wait before Thee,
Near to the heart of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There is a place of full release,
Near to the heart of God,
A place where all is joy and peace,
Near to the heart of God.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Sent from the heart of God,
Hold us, who wait before Thee,
Near to the heart of God.

hymns.title: Fill Thou my life, O Lord my God

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Not for the lip of praise alone,
I ask, but for a life made up

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Praise in the common things of life,
Praise in each duty and each deed,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Fill every part of me with praise;
Of Thee and of Thy love, O Lord,
Poor though I be and weak.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: So shall no part of day or night
But all my life, in every step,

hymns.title: If the path I travel
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: If there’s less of earth joy,
Let the tie that binds us,

hymns.title: Savior, lead me up the mountain
hymns.author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Where the strain of effort ceases,
Where in Christ we reign in Life.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Lead me higher up the mountain,
In Thy light I see the fountain,
And the blood it cleanses me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Savior, keep me up the mountain
Till, as one, we share Thine image,
And Thy love and grace extol.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Lead me higher up the mountain,
In Thy light I see the fountain,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Though I would, I cannot change,
By God’s law my sin’s revealed,
But the law of sin doth bind;
Though I struggle to be free,
No release my soul can find.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Many times I fall and rise,
Truly I am sold to sin
There’s no good within my flesh,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Now I know myself in part,
Nor to fleshly strength can cling;
All my trust and all my hope
Is in Jesus Christ my King.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: May the Cross put me to death
That on Christ I may rely;
May His death so work in me
That my self may be destroyed
And His life thru me may pour.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: O how bitter is my case!
Who this wretched slave can free,
Jesus shed His blood for me,
I receive Him as my life

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: When I come before the Lord.
Grace thru faith He gives to me!
Praise the Lord, He heard my cry
And has made me wholly free.

Not this way went the Crucified),
From all that dims Thy Calvary,
O Lamb of God, deliver me.

The faith that nothing can dismay,

hymns.title: O God, unblessing and unblest
hymns.author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: As smith, the iron, rough and cold,
So in Thy skillful hands, O take me,
And never let Thy love forsake me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Like rock uncrushed, the stubborn will,
Though bearing gold is barren still;
Like marble in the quarry rough,
The natural heart is useless stuff;
And so, I pray—“Do not forsake me,
But with Thy hand, O Savior, break me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: As mortars crush the hardest rock,
As hammers break the stony block,
As millstones bruise the finest wheat,
As nuts are broken for their meat,
So with Thy mighty hand, O break me,
And never let Thy love forsake me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Though crushed and broken, yet I’m nought
But fragments to the furnace brought;
Though bruised, I have no worth to feed
The multitudes that die in need;
And so, I pray—“Do not forsake me,
But meet for service, Savior, make me.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: As into useful forms the ore
From molten scraps the molders’ pour;
As fire doth make the bruised wheat,
When mixed and molded, fit to eat;
So, fit for use by fire, O make me,
And never let Thy love forsake me.”

hymns.author: Anonymous

lines: Deepen me, rid me of the superficial;

All the entangled in me quick unravel;

Enslave it with Thy matchless love,

It wants the breeze to nerve;

lines: My will is not my own
Till Thou hast made it Thine;
If it would reach the monarch’s throne

And fain I would: but though my will

Yet hindrances strew all the way;
I aim at Thee, yet from Thee stray.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: ’Tis mercy all, that Thou hast brought
My mind to seek her peace in Thee;
Yet, while I seek but find Thee not,
No peace my wand’ring soul shall see.
Oh, when shall all my wand’rings end,
And all my steps to Thee-ward tend!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Is there a thing beneath the sun
That strives with Thee my heart to share?
Ah! tear it thence, and reign alone,
The Lord of every motion there.
Then shall my heart from earth be free,
When it has found repose in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Oh, hide this self from me, that I
No more, but Christ in me may live;
Nor let one darling sin survive.
In all things nothing may I see,
Nothing desire or seek but Thee.

My heart which lowly waits Thy call;

“I am Thy Love, Thy God, Thy All.”
To feel Thy power, to hear Thy voice,
To taste Thy love, be all my choice.
