hymns.title: I’ve found the One of peerless worth
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio; Adapted from J. Mason
hymns.lyricist: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio; Adapted from J. Mason

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: And sing I must, for [G]Christ I [D]have:

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: My Christ, He is the Lamb of God,
He is the Sun of Righteousness,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: My Christ, He is the Tree of Life

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My Christ, He is the smitten Rock
He is the fountain in my heart

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ is my life, my light, my way,
My peace, my rest, my joy, my hope,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Christ is my wisdom and my pow’r,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Christ is my Savior, Shepherd, Lord,

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Christ is my Captain and my Guard,
My Bridegroom, Master and my Head;

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: Christ is my Prophet, Priest, and King;
My Priest that stands ’twixt me and God,
My King that rules with might.

sections.label: Verse 10
lines: Christ is the Author of my faith,

sections.label: Verse 12
lines: Christ is my sabbath and new moon,

sections.label: Verse 13
lines: Christ is my trust and my desire,
Who all my need doth meet.

sections.label: Verse 14
lines: My Christ what shall I call?
He is the first, He is the last,
My Christ is All in all.

sections.label: Verse 15
lines: Since such a treasure I possess,
My heart doth sing for joy;
And I must sing, and sing again;
Oh, what a Christ have I!

hymns.title: Jesus only is our message
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: All our guilt He bore away,
All our strength from day to day.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Jesus all in all we sing,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Saving us from self and sin,
And with all His Spirit’s fulness,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Jesus all in all we sing,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: And His risen life and fulness,
All His members still may share.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Jesus all in all we sing,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus, breathe Thy pow’r upon us,
Fill us with the Holy Ghost.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Jesus all in all we sing,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: And for Jesus we are waiting,

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: Jesus all in all we sing,

hymns.title: Jesus, Sun and Shield art Thou
hymns.author: Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus, Bread and Wine art Thou,
Never canst Thou cease to feed
Feed us still on bread divine,
Drink we still of heavenly wine.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus, Love and Life art Thou,
Ne’er to quicken shalt Thou cease,
All of life and love we need
Is in Thee, in Thee indeed.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus, Peace and Joy art Thou,
Joy that fades not, changes not,
Joy and Peace we have in Thee

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus, Song and Strength art Thou,
Still to us this strength and song,

hymns.title: Once it was the blessing
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Once I tried to use Him,

hymns.title: There is One amid all changes
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: It is [G]Christ the Rock of Ages,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: There is One whose arms upholdeth
Yet He bids us on His bosom
Let us bring them all to Jesus,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There is One whose love has kept us
And His hand will guard and guide us
Till all the storms are past;
Jesus, we will trust Thee ever,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: First and last, O Christ, we crown Thee,
Lord of lords, before Thy footstool
Haste the day when all shall crown Thee,

hymns.title: All is in Christ
hymns.author: Claire Lise de Benoit; Translated by Lois Thiessen
hymns.lyricist: Claire Lise de Benoit; Translated by Lois Thiessen

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: God’s dear Son is Lord of all.
By the shameful cross He bore.
By the Cross we have forgiveness,
By God’s Son is freely giv’n

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: God’s dear Son is Lord of all.
In me there is naught but weakness,
I am worthless, full of sin,
Now in Christ I find abundant
Savior, come and live in me,
Come and make me rich in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: God’s dear Son is Lord of all.
For my love is still so small;
Though I gave all my possessions,
This would profit scarce at all.
So I give myself, dear Master;
No thing hast Thou kept from me—
Nor will I keep aught from Thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Your whole self present to Him.
Vain your quest for lasting pleasure,
Christ alone must be your treasure,
Come, let Him disperse the famine
Let God’s Son, th’ Immortal King

hymns.title: Lord of all being, throned afar
hymns.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes (1809-1894)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Thy glory flames from sun and [A]star;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Sun of our life, Thy quickening ray
Sheds on our path the glow of day;
Star of our hope, Thy softened light
Cheers the long watches of the night.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Our midnight is Thy smile withdrawn,
Our noontide is Thy gracious dawn,
Our rainbow arch Thy mercy’s sign;
All, save the clouds of sin, are Thine.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord of all life, below, above,
Whose light is truth, whose warmth is love,
We ask no luster of our own.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Grant us Thy truth to make us free,
And kindling hearts that burn for Thee,
Till all Thy living altars claim
One holy light, one heavenly flame.

hymns.title: Jesus, my Savior, is all things to me
hymns.author: William James Kirkpatrick (1838-1921)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus in sickness, and Jesus in health,
Jesus in poverty, comfort or wealth;
Sunshine or tempest, whatever it be,
He is my safety—Jesus for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He is my Refuge, my Rock, and my Tower,
He is my Fortress, my Strength and my Pow’r;
Life everlasting, my Daysman is He,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: He is my Prophet, my Priest and my King,
He is my Bread of Life, Fountain and Spring;
Bright Sun of Righteousness, Daystar is He,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus in sorrow, in joy, or in pain,
Jesus my Treasure in loss or in gain;
Constant Companion where’er I may be,

hymns.title: Whom have I, Lord, in heav’n but Thee
hymns.author: R. George Halls

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: And this my song through [G]life shall [C]be:

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I envy not the rich their joys:
Christ for me! Christ for me!
I covet not earth’s glitt’ring toys:
Christ for me! Christ for me!
Earth can no lasting bliss bestow,
Mine is a joy no end can know:
Christ for me! Christ for me!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Though with the poor be cast my lot:
Christ for me! Christ for me!
Christ for me! Christ for me!
And death o’er flock and herd prevail,
Christ for me! Christ for me!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Though I am now on hostile ground,
Christ for me! Christ for me!
And sin beset me all around,
Christ for me! Christ for me!
Let earth her fiercest battles wage,
And foes against my soul engage,
Strong in His strength I scorn their rage:
Christ for me! Christ for me!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: And when my life draws to its close,
Christ for me! Christ for me!
Safe in His arms I shall repose,
Christ for me! Christ for me!
When sharpest pains my frame pervade,
And all the powers of nature fade,
Still will I sing through death’s cold shade;
Christ for me! Christ for me!

hymns.title: My heart is fixed, eternal God
hymns.author: Richard Jukes (1804-1867)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In Him I see the Godhead shine,
Christ for me, Christ for me;
Christ for me, Christ for me;
Who bore the guilt of man alone,
Christ for me, Christ for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Let others boast of heaps of gold,
Christ for me, Christ for me;
His riches never can be told,
Christ for me, Christ for me;
Your gold will waste and wear away,
Your honors perish in a day;
Christ for me, Christ for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In pining sickness, or in health,
Christ for me, Christ for me;
Christ for me, Christ for me;
When I the summons must obey,
And pass from this dark world away,
Christ for me, Christ for me.

hymns.title: None other Lamb, none other Name
hymns.author: Christina G. Rossetti

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: My faith burns low, my hope burns low;
Only my heart’s desire cries out in me
By the deep thunder of its want and woe,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, Thou art Life, though I be dead;
Love’s fire Thou art, however cold I be;
Nor heaven have I, nor place to lay my head,

hymns.title: I thank Thee, Lord, that Thou hast shown
hymns.author: Annie Wright Marston (1852-1937)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: That I might trust Thee so;
That Thou wouldst be so much to me.
In all the way I go,
That every need Thou wouldst supply.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I take Thee as my keeper now
My soul, my way, my works, my cause.
In Thy sole charge to be;
And my deposit, Thou, I know
Wilt guard secure from every foe.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I take Thee for my peace, O Lord.
My heart to keep and fill
Thine own great calm, amid earth’s storms
And as Thy kingdom doth increase,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: I take Thee as my wisdom too
Thou, who dost choose the foolish things.
That I may speak and work for Thee
As Thou shalt work and speak in me.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: I take Thee, Lord, to be my all.
Since all Thou art is mine;
I nothing have, and nothing am;
Thou shalt be everything to me

hymns.title: O Christ, in Thee my soul hath found
hymns.author: Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]O Christ, in Thee my soul hath found,
The peace, the joy I sought so long,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I sighed for rest and happiness,
I yearned for them, not Thee;
But, while I passed my Savior by,
His love laid hold on me.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Now none but Christ can satisfy,
There’s love and life and lasting joy,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I tried the broken cisterns, Lord,
E’en as I stooped to drink they fled,
And mocked me as I wailed.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Now none but Christ can satisfy,
There’s love and life and lasting joy,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The pleasures lost I sadly mourned,
Till grace the sightless eyes received,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Now none but Christ can satisfy,
There’s love and life and lasting joy,

hymns.title: I have come to the Fountain of Life
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I have come to the Fountain of Blood
That for guilt and uncleanness doth flow;
I have washed in its sin-cleansing flood
And my garments are whiter than snow.
I count not my righteousness mine—
’Tis Jesus that lives in my soul.
I partake of His nature divine,
And in Him I am perfectly whole.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Oh, come to the Fountain of Life,
The fountain that never runs dry;
Oh, drink of the boundless supply,
For Christ is the Fountain of Life.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I have come to the Fountain of Health,
’Tis a secret man’s wisdom or wealth
But the secret my Lord hath revealed
In the fountain that flows from His side,
In the stripes by whose pain we are healed,
In Himself as He comes to abide.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Oh, come to the Fountain of Life,
The fountain that never runs dry;
Oh, drink of the boundless supply,
For Christ is the Fountain of Life.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I have come to the Fountain of Joy;
His joy is the strength of my heart.
My delight is unmixed with alloy,
The fig tree may wither and die,
But my fountains can never be dry—
My portion, my joy is divine.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Oh, come to the Fountain of Life,
The fountain that never runs dry;
Oh, drink of the boundless supply,
For Christ is the Fountain of Life.

hymns.title: I have found, I have found the way
hymns.author: Theodore Monod (1836-1921)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He hath taken our sins away,
When on Calv’ry’s cross He bled;
The disease of our soul He heals
Though Satan hath pierced us deep,
And great the grace each prays;
The more we prove His might,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Long, alas! in the gloom I fought,
Jesus seemed only this to me:
But sweet are the light and calm

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O my Sun and my Shield art Thou
Lead on where Thou hast trod;
My Salvation, my Joy, my Song,
My Brother, and yet my God.
I now can trust and praise;

hymns.title: Jesus, Fountain of my days
hymns.author: George Matheson (1842-1906)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, how weary were the years
Ere Thy form to me was known;
Oh, how gloomy were the fears
When I seemed to be alone;
I despaired the storm to brave
Till Thy footprints touched the wave.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: But Thy presence on the deep
Calmed the pulses of the sea,
And the waters sank to sleep
In the rest of seeing Thee;
Heard the mandate, Peace, be still!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Now Thy will and mine are one,
Heart in heart, and hand in hand;
All the clouds have touched the sun,
And the ships have reached the land;
For Thy love has said to me,
No more night! and No more sea!

hymns.title: Lord, Thou hast made Thyself to me
hymns.author: Charlotte Elliott (1789-1871)
hymns.composer: Henri Frederick Hemy (1818-1888); Adapted by James George Walton (1821-1905)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: And Thou, blest vision of my soul,
Hast made my broken nature whole;
My nature Thou hast lifted up,
And filled me with a glorious hope.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Nearer and dearer still to me,
Brighter the vision of Thy face,
More charming still Thy words of grace;
So, life shall be transformed to love,
Thy grace and mercy more to prove.

hymns.title: The Lord’s my Shepherd, I’ll not want
hymns.author: W. Whittingham; F. Rous

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: My soul He doth restore again,
And me to walk doth make
E’en for His own name’s sake.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Yea, though I walk in death’s dark vale,
Yet will I fear no ill;
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My head Thou dost with oil anoint,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Goodness and mercy all my life

hymns.title: The King of love my Shepherd is
hymns.author: Henry Williams Baker (1821-1877)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Where streams of living water flow
And, where the verdant pastures grow,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Perverse and foolish oft I strayed,
But yet in love He sought me,
And on His shoulder gently laid,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In death’s dark vale I fear no ill
With Thee, dear Lord, beside me;
Thy rod and staff my comfort still,
Thy Cross before to guide me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou spread’st a table in my sight;
And oh, what transport of delight

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: And so through all the length of days
Good Shepherd, may I sing Thy praise

hymns.title: How tedious and tasteless the hours
hymns.author: John Newton (1725-1807)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: His name yields the richest perfume,
And sweeter than music His voice;
And makes all within me rejoice.
I should, were He always thus nigh,
Have nothing to wish or to fear;
No mortal so happy as I;
My summer would last all the year.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: My all to His pleasure resigned;
No changes of season or place,
Would make any change in my mind.
While blessed with a sense of His love,
A palace a toy would appear;
If Jesus would dwell with me there.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My Lord, if indeed I am Thine,
If Thou art my sun and my song,
Say, why do I languish and pine?
And why are my winters so long?
Oh, drive these dark clouds from the sky,
Or take me to Thee up on high,
Where winter and clouds are no more.

hymns.title: Jesus is all the world to me
hymns.author: Will Lamartine Thompson (1847-1909)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: He [D]is my strength from [G]day to day;
When I am [C]sad, He makes me [G]glad;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus is all the world to me,
I go to Him for blessings, and
He gives them o’er and o’er.
He sends the sunshine and the rain;
He sends the harvest’s golden grain:
Sunshine and rain, harvest of grain—

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus is all the world to me,
And true to Him I’ll be.
Oh, how could I this Friend deny
When He’s so true to me?
Following Him I know I’m right;
He watches o’er me day and night.
Following Him by day and night,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus is all the world to me,
I trust Him now; I’ll trust Him when
Beautiful life with such a Friend;
Beautiful life that has no end!

hymns.title: Fade, fade each earthly joy
hymns.author: Jane Catharine Bonar (1821-1884)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Born but for one brief day,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All that my soul has tried

hymns.title: Thou hidden source of calm repose
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus, my All in all Thou art,
My rest in toil, mine ease in pain;
The med’cine of my broken heart;
In war, my peace; in loss, my gain;
My smile beneath the tyrant’s frown;
In shame, my glory and my crown.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: My light in Satan’s darkest hour;
My life in death; my Lord, my all.

hymns.title: For every sin however deep
hymns.author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: For every trial great or small,
For every care that would appall,
For all the stumbling feet that fall,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: When earthly things bring sweet delight,
When all is well, and skies are bright,
When ease would cloud the heavenly light,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: When sorrow darkens all the day,
When hearts are numb and cannot pray,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Help me in all Thy hand to see,
So wilt Thou then be unto me,

hymns.title: The Savior can lift every burden
hymns.author: Oswald Jeffrey Smith (1889-1986)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The Savior can bear every sorrow,
In Him there is comfort and rest;
No matter how great the affliction,
He only permits what is best.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: The Savior can solve every problem,
The tangles of life can undo;
There is nothing too hard for Jesus,
There is nothing that He cannot do.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Savior can strengthen the weary,
His grace is sufficient for all;
He knows every step of the pathway
And listens to hear when we call.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: The Savior can solve every problem,
The tangles of life can undo;
There is nothing too hard for Jesus,
There is nothing that He cannot do.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The Savior can break sin’s dominion,
The vict’ry He won long ago;
In Him there is freedom from bondage,
He’s able to conquer the foe.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: The Savior can solve every problem,
The tangles of life can undo;
There is nothing too hard for Jesus,
There is nothing that He cannot do.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: The heart that the world cannot fill;
The soul that is yielded and still.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: The Savior can solve every problem,
The tangles of life can undo;
There is nothing too hard for Jesus,
There is nothing that He cannot do.

hymns.title: All things are possible to him
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio
hymns.composer: Henri Frederick Hemy (1818-1888); Adapted by James George Walton (1821-1905)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: That here sin’s reign in me should cease;
Yet shall it be, I know it shall;
If nothing is too hard for Thee,
All things are possible to me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Though earth and hell the Word gainsay,
The Word of God shall never fail;
The Lord can break sin’s iron sway;
All things are possible to me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: All things are possible to God;
To Christ, the power of God in man;
To me when I am all renewed,
In Christ am fully formed again,
And from the reign of sin set free,
All things are possible to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: All things are possible to God;
To Christ, the power of God in me;
Now shed Thy mighty Self abroad,
Let me no longer live, but Thee;
Give me this hour in Thee to prove

hymns.title: Objective and subjective Christ is to us
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In heaven He sits at the right hand of God,
Where as the High Priest He presented His blood;
Our Advocate, bearing our burdens above,
Our Surety, He careth for us in His love.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He now is the Spirit, our spirit within;
He’s there as our life, all things bringing with Him;
He’s there as our strength and our grace every hour,
Our Paraclete in us, sustaining with pow’r.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In heaven for us He’s the glorified man,
The Forerunner entered, fulfilling God’s plan;
Man into God bringing and making him one
With God in the heav’nlies, in Him as the Son.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: In us all the fulness of God dwells in Him;
As Spirit He brings God Himself thus within,
Revealing and making God real unto us,
God one with us building in life glorious.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: The Savior ascended in heaven now dwells,
And soon He’s returning for us His Word tells;
Deliverer indwelling, He now in us lives,
And soon will transfigure, His glory to give.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: The day soon is coming when heaven and earth
Will mingle in one in that city of worth;
Objective and subjective will in that day
Be mingled within us in glory for aye.

hymns.title: Christ to me is so subjective
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Christ to me is so subjective,
As the Spirit He revives me

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: So subjective is my Christ to me!
Real in me, and rich and sweet!
All-inclusive is my Christ to me!
All my needs He fully meets.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ to me is so subjective,
By the mind and will renewing

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: So subjective is my Christ to me!
Real in me, and rich and sweet!
All-inclusive is my Christ to me!
All my needs He fully meets.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Christ to me is so subjective,
By the law of life and power

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: So subjective is my Christ to me!
Real in me, and rich and sweet!
All-inclusive is my Christ to me!
All my needs He fully meets.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ to me is so subjective,
He corrects and rules and guides me,

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: So subjective is my Christ to me!
Real in me, and rich and sweet!
All-inclusive is my Christ to me!
All my needs He fully meets.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Christ to me is so subjective,
With His riches He supplies me,

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: So subjective is my Christ to me!
Real in me, and rich and sweet!
All-inclusive is my Christ to me!
All my needs He fully meets.

hymns.title: It is God’s intent and pleasure
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ may live in me;

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be wrought in me;
But His Christ my all to be.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be formed in me;
Not the outward forms to follow,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be wrought in me;
But His Christ my all to be.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ make home in me;
Not just outwardly to serve Him,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be wrought in me;
But His Christ my all to be.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ my hope may be;

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be wrought in me;
But His Christ my all to be.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be all in me;

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: It is God’s intent and pleasure
That His Christ be wrought in me;
But His Christ my all to be.

hymns.title: O Lord, Thou art in me as life
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [C]O Lord, Thou art in me as life

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: To all my needs both great and small

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: O Lord, Thou art the Spirit!
How dear and near to me!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy sweet anointing with Thy might

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: O Lord, Thou art the Spirit!
How dear and near to me!

sections.label: Verse 4

One spirit with me all the time

hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

To its claims I’m ever dead;
Nevermore the law shall bind me,
But by grace I’ll live instead.

Now it has no ground within me,
I am freed from all its sway.

sections.label: Chorus 3

lines: Christ has made me more than conqu’ror,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ through death has crushed the devil,
World and demons by His might,
From the pow’r of darkness brought me

sections.label: Chorus 4

sections.label: Verse 5

Or their depth and height unmeasured,
Yet they are my joy and strength.

sections.label: Chorus 5

That Thou, the Word, didst stoop to take

sections.label: Verse 6

hymns.title: Lord Jesus, I love Thee, I know Thou art mine
hymns.author: William Ralph Featherstone (1846-1873)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I love Thee, because Thou hast first loved me,
And purchased my pardon on Calvary’s tree;
I love Thee for wearing the thorns on Thy brow;
If ever I loved Thee, Lord Jesus, ’tis now.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I’ll love Thee in life, I will love Thee in death,
And praise Thee as long as Thou lendest me breath;
And say when the death-dew lies cold on my brow,
If ever I loved Thee, Lord Jesus, ’tis now.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In ages eternal of endless delight
I’ll ever adore Thee in glory so bright;
I’ll sing with the glittering crown on my brow,
If ever I loved Thee, Lord Jesus, ’tis now.

hymns.title: When this passing world is done
hymns.author: Robert Murray McCheyne (1813-1843)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When I stand before the throne
Dressed in beauty not my own,
When I see Thee as Thou art,
Then, Lord, shall I fully know,
Not till then, how much I owe.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: E’en on earth, as through a glass
Make Thy Spirit’s help so meet:
E’en on earth, Lord, make me know
Something of how much I owe.

hymns.title: I love my Lord, but with no love of mine
hymns.author: Madame Jeanne-Marie Bouvier de la Motte-Guyon (1648-1717) bio
hymns.lyricist: Madame Jeanne-Marie Bouvier de la Motte-Guyon (1648-1717) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]I love my Lord, but with no [C]love of [G]mine,
I love Thee, Lord, but all the [C]love is [G]Thine,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou, Lord, alone, art all Thy children need,
From Thee the streams of blessedness proceed,
Fountain of life, and all-abounding grace,
Our source, our center, and our dwelling-place.

hymns.title: Something every heart is loving
hymns.author: Gerhardt Tersteegen (1697-1769); Translated by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)
hymns.lyricist: Gerhardt Tersteegen (1697-1769); Translated by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Thus I cast the world behind me;
Beauteous more than all things beauteous,
He alone is joy to me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Is the glory of Thy face;
Thou art loving, sweet, and tender,
Full of pity, full of grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: When I hated, Thou didst love me,
Shedd’st for me Thy precious blood;
Shall I not love Thee, my God?

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Keep my heart still faithful to Thee,
That my earthly life may be
But a shadow to that glory
Of my hidden life in Thee.

hymns.title: Earthen vessel I was made
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In His image I was made,
Fit that Christ should all pervade;
Thus the vessel God did form

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: As the Spirit one with me,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Moving in me day by day,
Mingling with me all the way,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: That He may be shown thru me.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: That the clay may change in form,

hymns.title: Enter the veil and go without the camp
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Taste heaven's [G]sweetness, thus the earth for[A]sake;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Enter the veil and go without the camp,
By heaven’s presence will the earth depart;
If heaven’s glory doth my spirit charm,
How can earth’s happiness possess my heart?

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Enter the veil, behold the glorious Christ,
Go out the camp to Jesus, let Him lead;
If throne and crown my spirit here enthrall,
Manger and cross cannot my steps impede.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Enter the veil for resurrection pow’r,
Go out the camp to bear the cross and woe,
If I His radiant face in heaven see,
His footsteps I will follow here below.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Enter the veil, on heaven’s fatness feast,
Without the camp, in hardship persevere;
Though earthly trials sorely pain my heart,
Heaven’s communion doth my spirit cheer.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Enter the veil, Christ’s riches there enjoy,
Without the camp, the needs of men supply;
The life of heaven living out thru me
The souls of earth will bless and satisfy.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Enter the veil till it exists no more,
Go out the camp till all the camps are gone;
Until the heavens and the earth unite,
Till God and man together dwell in one.

hymns.title: Through Thy precious body broken
hymns.author: Elizabeth Dark

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When we see Thy love unshaken—
Scorned by man, by God forsaken—
Thy loved cross alone can charm us;
Shame need now no more alarm us;
Glad we follow, nought can harm us—

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Lamb of God, through Thee we enter—
Cleansed by Thee, we boldly venture—
Not a stain; a new creation:
Ours is such a full salvation;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Forth we hasten, fear no danger—
Drawn by love that knows no measure—

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Soon Thy saints shall all be gathered—
All with Thee—no more be scattered—
Nought from Thee, our hearts shall sever;
We shall see Thee; grieve Thee never;

hymns.title: I’ve believed the true report
hymns.author: Charles Price Jones (1865-1949)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: I have passed the outer court,
To the world and sin I've died,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I’m a king and priest to God,
By the cleansing of the blood,
By the Spirit’s pow’r and light,
I am living day and night,
In the holiest place so bright,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: I have passed the riven veil,
I am living in the presence

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I have passed the outer veil,
Which did once God’s light conceal,
But the blood has brought me in
Where there’s death to self and sin,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: I have passed the riven veil,
I am living in the presence

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I have passed the inner veil,
By the power of the blood,
Now the Lord is my abode

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: I have passed the riven veil,
I am living in the presence

hymns.title: Marvel not that Christ in glory
hymns.author: Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I have seen a light from heaven
Past the brightness of the sun—
Light that knows no cloud, no waning,
Light wherein I see His face,
All the riches of His grace:

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All the wonders of His glory,
How for me He won, He keepeth
But within the veil to dwell,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I have seen the face of Jesus—
Tell me not of aught beside;
I have heard the voice of Jesus—
In the radiance of the glory
First I saw His blessed face,

hymns.title: In the secret of His presence
hymns.author: Ellen Lakshmi Goreh (1853-?)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When my soul is faint and thirsty,
There is cool and pleasant shelter,
And a fresh and crystal spring;
And my Savior rests beside me,
If I tried, I could not utter
What He says when thus we meet.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Only this I know: I tell Him
All my doubts and griefs and fears;
And my drooping soul He cheers;
Do you think He ne’er reproves me?
What a false friend He would be,
If He never, never told me
Of the sins which He must see.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Would you like to know that sweetness
Of the secret of the Lord?
Go and hide beneath His shadow;
This shall then be your reward;
And whene’er you leave the silence
By the Spirit bear the image
Of the Master in your face.

hymns.title: I come to His presence afresh
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: And His [D]face I see as it [G]shines on me—
And He [G]speaks to me and re[D]veals to me
And with sweet de[B7]light I par[Em]take of [C]Him,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: As Spirit He speaks thru the Word
Till my heart in echo is singing,
And the fount of life with His grace and pow’r
And He speaks to me and reveals to me
All His riches for me today;
And I drink of Him for my every need,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: In tenderness He deals with me,
While I stay with joy in His presence;
And He saturates and supplies my soul
And He speaks to me and reveals to me
All His riches for me today;
And in every way I partake of Him,

hymns.title: Still, still with Thee, when purple morning breaketh
hymns.author: Harriet Beecher Stowe (1812-1896)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Dawns the sweet conscious[A7]ness, I am with [D]Thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: As in the dawning, o’er the waveless ocean,
The image of the morning star doth rest,
So in this stillness Thou beholdest only
Thine image in the waters of my breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: When sinks the soul, subdued by toil, to slumber,
Its closing eye looks up to Thee in prayer;
Sweet the repose, beneath Thy wings o’ershadowing,
But sweeter still to wake and find Thee there.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: So shall it be at last, in that bright morning
When the soul waketh, and life’s shadows flee;
Oh, in that hour, fairer than daylight’s dawning,
Shall rise the glorious thought, I am with Thee!

hymns.title: Thy name is sweet as ointment poured forth
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He’s my Beloved, I am His own love;
He draweth me, pursue I after Him.
Fragrant as myrrh, I’d hide Him in my heart;
Beauteous as henna*, I’d be clothed with Him;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Bathe in His love, and of His fatness taste,
Lie on His breast, His sweetness there enjoy;
His love the banner, His affection shown
Tenderly soothes my heart to purest joy.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh, my Beloved’s mine, and I am His;
I am a lily and my Shepherd He;
May daybreak come, the shadows flee away,
Him on the mountains as a hart I’d see.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Myrrh of the death with Him and frankincense,
North wind awake, and let the south wind blow,
Make my heart’s garden pleasure to His heart.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: I’d be to Him a dove that’s undefiled,
As a pure lily in His presence be,
His, wholly His, the joy of all His joys,
He wholly mine, the Song of songs to me.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Fair as the moon, conformed to Him I’d be,
Clear as the sun, unto His stature grown;
For my Beloved, all to please His heart,
For my Beloved, that His life be shown.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Thou art my life, and I Thine image real;
Love in such union is as death most strong,
Ne’er can it be destroyed or e’er replaced
Till Thou on spices mountains come ere long.

hymns.title: Jesus Himself drew near
hymns.author: Ada Ruth Habershon (1861-1918)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: And soon their [D7]hearts be[Em]gan to burn,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When He was walking at their side,
How could they but be glad?

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And all their doubts were solved;
He showed them why Christ came to die,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: They could not let Him leave them thus,

hymns.title: Leaning on the Everlasting Arms
hymns.author: Elisha Albright Hoffman (1839-1929)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O how sweet to walk in this pilgrim way,
O how bright the path grows from day to day,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Safe and secure from all alarms;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: What have I to dread, what have I to fear,
I have peace complete with my Lord so near,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Safe and secure from all alarms;

hymns.title: Savior, I by faith am touching Thee
hymns.author: Bertha Fennell

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Touching Thee in faith, I take Thee
In Thy riches full and free;
All I am I open to Thee,
All Thou art Thou giv’st to me.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Touching Thee, new life is glowing

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O most mighty King of kings;
High I mount on eagle wings.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Touching Thee, new life is glowing

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Grace and virtue, strength and wisdom,
All my need, by Thee supplied;
Keep me touching, keep me claiming,
Keep me ever at Thy side.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Touching Thee, new life is glowing

hymns.title: Come, O Thou Traveler unknown
hymns.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I need not tell Thee who I am,
Thyself hast called me by my name,
Look on Thy hands, and read it there;
But who, I ask Thee, who art Thou?
Tell me Thy name, and tell me now.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: In vain Thou strugglest to get free;
I never will unloose my hold;
Art Thou the Man that died for me?
The secret of Thy love unfold;
Wrestling, I will not let Thee go,
Till I Thy name, Thy nature know.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Yield to me now, for I am weak,
Speak to my heart, in blessings speak,
Be conquered by my instant prayer;
Speak, or Thou never hence shalt move,
And tell me if Thy name be Love.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: ’Tis Love! ’tis Love! Thou diedst for me,
I hear Thy whisper in my heart;
The morning breaks, the shadows flee:
To me, to all Thy mercies move;
Thy nature and Thy name is Love.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Lame as I am, I take the prey;
Hell, earth and sin, with ease o’ercome.
I leap for joy, pursue my way,
And, as a bounding hart, I run,
Thy nature and Thy name is Love.

hymns.title: Thou hast said Thou art the Vine, Lord
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [Dm]Thou hast said Thou art the [A]Vine, Lord,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Bearing fruit is my deep longing,
To Thy throne to bring more glory,
That Thy will may be expressed.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: But I fail to understand, Lord,
More I feel I’m not in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: How I feel I’m not abiding;
Though I pray and strongly will,
Yet from me Thou seemest distant
And my life is barren still.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Yet Thou art the Vine, Thou saidst it.
And I am a branch in Thee;
When I take Thee as my Savior.
Then this fact is wrought in me.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Now I’m in Thee and I need not
For I’m joined to Thee already,
With Thy flesh and bones I’m one.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Not to “go in” is the secret.
That I ne’er may leave I’d ask Thee.
Not how I may get within.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: I am in, already in Thee!
What a place to which I’m brought!
There’s no need for prayer or struggling,
God Himself the work has wrought.

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: Since I’m in, why ask to enter;
Now with praise and much rejoicing
For Thy Word, I dwell therein.

sections.label: Verse 10
lines: Now in Thee I rest completely,
Thou art life and Thou art power,
All in all to me Thou art.

hymns.title: Abiding, oh, so wondrous sweet
hymns.author: C. B. J. Root

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He speaks, and by His word is giv’n
His peace, a blessed gift of heav’n;
Not as the world He peace doth give,
’Tis through this hope my soul shall live.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I live; not I; ’tis He alone
By whom the mighty work is done;
Dead to myself, alive to Him,
I count all loss His rest to gain.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Now rest, my heart, the work is done,
I’m saved through the Eternal Son;
Let all my pow’rs my soul employ,
To tell the world my peace and joy.

hymns.title: Abide in Thee! in that deep love of Thine
hymns.author: J. Denham Smith

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Abide in Thee! my Savior God, I know
How love of Thine so vast in me may flow,
My empty vessel, running o’er with joy,
Must overflow to Thee without alloy.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Abide in Thee! nor doubt, nor self, nor sin,
Can e’er prevail with Thy blest life within;
Joined to Thyself, communing deep, my soul
Knows naught besides its motions to control.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Abide in Thee! ’tis thus I only know
The secrets of Thy mind e’en while below—
All joy and peace, and knowledge of Thy word,
All pow’r and fruit, and service for the Lord.

hymns.title: I have learned the wondrous secret
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Chorus
lines: [A]I am [D]hiding in the bosom of His [E7]love.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: And He lives and dwells with me;
I have ceased from all my struggling,
All my will is yielding to Him,
And His precious blood each moment
Keeps me cleansed and free from sin.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: I am hiding in the bosom of His love.
I am hiding in the bosom of His love.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All my sicknesses I bring Him,
And He bears them all away;
All my fears and griefs I tell Him,
All my cares from day to day,
All my strength I draw from Jesus,
By His breath I live and move;
E’en His very mind He gives me,
And His faith, and life, and love.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: I am hiding in the bosom of His love.
I am hiding in the bosom of His love.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: For my words I take His wisdom,
For my works His Spirit’s power;
For my ways His ceaseless presence
Guards and guides me every hour.
Of my heart, He is the portion,
Of my joy the boundless spring;

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: I am hiding in the bosom of His love.
I am hiding in the bosom of His love.

hymns.title: Under His wings I am safely abiding
hymns.author: William Orcutt Cushing (1823-1902)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Still I can trust Him, I [F]know He will [C]keep me;
[F]He has re[C]deemed me, and [G7]I am His [C]child.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Under His wings—what a refuge in sorrow!
How the heart yearningly turns to His rest!
Often when earth has no balm for my healing,
There I find comfort, and there I am blest.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Under His wings, under His wings,
Who from His love can sever?
Under His wings my soul shall abide,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Under His wings—oh, what precious enjoyment!
There will I hide till life’s trials are o’er;
Sheltered, protected, no evil can harm me;
Resting in Jesus I’m safe evermore.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Under His wings, under His wings,
Who from His love can sever?
Under His wings my soul shall abide,

hymns.title: Oh, safe to the Rock that is higher than I
hymns.author: William Orcutt Cushing (1823-1902)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [A7]Oh, [D]safe to the Rock that is [G]high[A7]er than [D]I,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In the calm of the noontide, in sorrow’s lone hour,
In times when temptation casts o’er me its power;
In the tempests of life, on its wide, heaving sea,
Thou blest Rock of Ages, I’m hiding in Thee.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Hiding in Thee, hiding in Thee,
Thou blest Rock of Ages, I’m hiding in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: How oft in the conflict, when pressed by the foe,
I have fled to my Refuge and breathed out my woe,,
How often, when trials like sea-billows roll,
Have I hidden in Thee, O Thou Rock of my soul.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Hiding in Thee, hiding in Thee,
Thou blest Rock of Ages, I’m hiding in Thee.

hymns.title: O Lamb of God, still keep me
hymns.author: James George Deck (1807-1884)
hymns.composer: From Little Flock Hymns with Optional Tunes

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: What foes and snares surround me,
The grace that sought and found me

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In all its care and woe.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Soon shall my eyes behold Thee,
One half hath not been told me
Of all Thy power and grace;

hymns.title: Tis so sweet to trust in Jesus
hymns.author: Louisa M. R. Stead (circa 1850-1917)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O how sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just to trust His cleansing blood;
Just in simple faith to plunge me,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him,
How I’ve proved Him o’er and o’er,
O for grace to trust Him more.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Yes, ’tis sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just from sin and self to cease;
Life, and rest, and joy, and peace.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him,
How I’ve proved Him o’er and o’er,
O for grace to trust Him more.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I’m so glad I learned to trust Thee,
And I know that Thou art with me,
Wilt be with me to the end.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him,
How I’ve proved Him o’er and o’er,
O for grace to trust Him more.

hymns.title: Simply trusting every day
hymns.author: Edgar Page Stites (1836-1921)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Into this poor heart of mine;
While He leads I cannot fall,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Trusting as the days go by,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Singing if my way be clear,
Praying if the path be drear;
If in danger, for Him call,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Trusting as the days go by,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Trusting Him while life shall last,
Trusting Him till earth is past,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Trusting as the days go by,

hymns.title: All my doubts I give to Jesus
hymns.author: J. C. Morgan

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: All my sins I lay on Jesus,
He doth wash me in His blood,
He will keep me pure and holy,
He will keep me close to God.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All my fears I give to Jesus,
Rests my weary soul on Him;
Though my way be hid in darkness,
Never can His light grow dim.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: All my joys I give to Jesus,
He is all I want of bliss;
He of all the worlds is Master;
He has all I need in this.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: All I am I give to Jesus;
All my body, all my soul;
All l have, and all I hope for,

hymns.title: Thou whose name is called Jesus
hymns.author: Jean Sophia Pigott (1845-1882)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou canst keep my feet from falling,
Thou who dost present me faultless

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All the sin in me, my Savior,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou canst keep me upward looking,
Thou canst make me stand, upholden
By the greatness of Thy grace;
Now I claim from Thee, dear Lord.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Oh! what joy to trust Thee, Jesus,
And to learn amid earth’s shadows
Only those who prove Thee know
What the grace Thou dost bestow.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Make my life a bright outshining
Of Thy life, that all may see

hymns.title: Jesus hath died and hath risen again
hymns.author: Arthur Cleveland Downer

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Sin’s condemnation is over and gone,
Life and salvation my soul hath put on:

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Yes, Jesus saves me all the time;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Satan may tempt, but he never shall reign,
Doubts I have buried, and this is my strain,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Yes, Jesus saves me all the time;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Resting in Jesus, abiding in Him,
Never again need my pathway be dim:

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Yes, Jesus saves me all the time;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus is stronger than Satan and sin,
Therefore I triumph without and within:

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Yes, Jesus saves me all the time;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Sorrow and pain may beset me about,
Battling in faith, I can joyfully shout:

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: Yes, Jesus saves me all the time;

hymns.title: Once I thought I walked with Jesus
hymns.author: Francis Augustus Blackmer (1855-1930)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: But He call’d me closer to Him,
And when I had fully yielded,
Filled my soul with perfect peace.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Oh, the peace the Savior gives!
And my way has brighter grown
Since I’ve learned to trust Him more.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And the Savior bears me gently
O’er those places once so rough.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Oh, the peace the Savior gives!
And my way has brighter grown
Since I’ve learned to trust Him more.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Day by day my soul He’s keeping
And my heart is full of singing
To my Savior from all sin.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Oh, the peace the Savior gives!
And my way has brighter grown
Since I’ve learned to trust Him more.

hymns.title: Lord Jesus, Thou dost keep Thy child
hymns.author: Jean Sophia Pigott (1845-1882)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O glorious Savior, Thee I praise;
To Thee my new glad song I raise,
And tell of what Thou art.
Thy grace is boundless in its store;
Thy face of love shines evermore;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Trusting in Thee: Thine own right hand
My soul doth triumph in Thy word;
Thine, Thine be all the praise, dear Lord,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy power doth save me from my sins;
This life of trust, how glad, how sweet;
My need and Thy great fulness meet,
And I have all in Thee.

hymns.title: I take Thy promise, Lord, in all its length
hymns.author: Henry Legh Richmond Deck (1853-1910)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: And breadth and [G]fulness, as my daily [A]strength;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Days may be coming fraught with loss and change,
New scenes surround my life and fancies strange;
I thank Thee that no day can ever break,
Savior, when Thou wilt leave me or forsake.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There may be days of darkness and distress,
When sin has power to tempt, and care to press,
Yet in the darkest day I will not fear,
For, ’mid the shadows, Thou wilt still be near.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Days there may be of joy and deep delight,
When earth seems fairest, and her skies most bright,
Then draw me closer to Thee, lest I rest
Elsewhere, my Savior, than upon Thy breast.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: And all the other days that make my life,
Marked by no special joy or grief or strife,
Days filled with quiet duties, trivial care,
Burdens too small for other hearts to share;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Spend Thou these days with me, all shall be Thine,
So shall the darkest hour with glory shine.
Then when these earthly years have passed away,
Let me be with Thee in the perfect day.

hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 1

sections.label: Chorus 4

I praise Him that my prayer is heard,
And claim my answer from the Lord,

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: And Thou, according to Thy word,

hymns.title: When I fear my faith will fail
hymns.author: Ada Ruth Habershon (1861-1918)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I could never keep my hold,
For my love is often cold,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: For my Savior loves me so,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I am precious in His sight,
Those He saves are His delight,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: For my Savior loves me so,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: He’ll not let my soul be lost,
Bought by Him at such a cost,

sections.label: Chorus 4

hymns.title: My will is weak, my strength is frail
hymns.author: Adapted from Samuel H. Wilkinson (1914); Translated from Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio
hymns.lyricist: Adapted from Samuel H. Wilkinson (1914); Translated from Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]My will is weak, my [A]strength is frail,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I’ve tried my best, but still have failed,
E’en as before I’ve failed and erred;
Thy patience is my only trust
To hold and keep me to Thy word.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Whene’er my heart is lifted up,
How very near I am to fall;
I dare not do, I dare not think,
I need Thyself in great or small.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou art my Savior, strength and stay,
O Lord, I come to seek Thy face;
Though I’m the weakest of the weak,
My strength is nothing but Thy grace.

hymns.title: Jesus! I am resting, resting
hymns.author: Jean Sophia Pigott (1845-1882)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: In the joy of [D]what Thou art;

sections.label: Chorus
lines: In the joy of [D]what Thou art;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, how great Thy loving kindness,
Yes, I rest in Thee, Beloved,
Know what wealth of grace is Thine,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: In the joy of what Thou art;
I am finding out the greatness

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I behold Thee as Thou art,
And Thy love, so pure, so changeless,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: In the joy of what Thou art;
I am finding out the greatness

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Ever lift Thy face upon me,
As I work and wait for Thee;

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: In the joy of what Thou art;
I am finding out the greatness

hymns.title: Resting on the faithfulness of Christ our Lord
hymns.author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1836-1879)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [C]Resting on the fulness of His [G]own sure [D7]word,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Resting ’neath His guiding hand for untrack’d days,
Resting ’neath His shadow from the noontide rays,
Resting at the eventide beneath His wing,
In the glorious presence of our Savior King.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Resting in the fortress while the foe is nigh,
Resting in the lifeboat while the waves roll high,
Resting in His chariot for the swift, glad race,
Resting, always resting, in His boundless grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Resting in the pastures and beneath the Rock,
Resting by the waters where He leads His flock,
Resting, while we listen, at His glorious feet,
Resting in His very arms, oh, rest complete!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Resting and believing, let us onward press;
Resting on Himself, the Lord our righteousness;
Resting and rejoicing, let His saved ones sing,
Glory, glory, glory be to Christ our King!

hymns.title: On Thee my heart is resting
hymns.author: Theodore Monod (1836-1921)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: My guilt is great, but greater
Hast died that I should live.
Thy blood is all my treasure,
Thy word is all my trust.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: On Thee my heart is resting,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: What though I be but weakness?
My strength is not in me;

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: On Thee my heart is resting,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: When clouds are darkest round me,
Thou, Lord, art then most near,
In vain my foes would drive me

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: On Thee my heart is resting,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: To whom shall I give glory
Thy grace shall still be with me,
Thy grace, to live and die.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: On Thee my heart is resting,

hymns.title: Trust and obey
hymns.author: John Henry Sammis (1846-1919)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Not a cloud in the skies,
But His smile quickly drives it away;
Not a doubt or a fear,
Not a sigh or a tear,
Can abide while we trust and obey.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: But our toil He doth richly repay;
Not a grief or a loss,
Not a frown or a cross,
But is blest if we trust and obey.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Until all on the altar we lay;
Are for them who will trust and obey.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: We will sit at His feet,
Or we’ll walk by His side in the way;
What He says we will do;
Where He sends, we will go,
Never fear, only trust and obey.

hymns.title: Go to Him without the camp
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Willing e’en to bear the cross;
He has trod the narrow way,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He the Father’s will did mind,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Though the path be lone and grim;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: There to walk with Him, how blest!
E’er to see His smiling face

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Till the dawning of the day;
Then I’ll see Him and rejoice,
With Him in His kingdom stay.

hymns.title: Anywhere with Jesus I can safely go
hymns.author: Jessie Brown Pounds (1861-1921)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G7]Anywhere He leads me in this world be[F]low.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Anywhere with Jesus I am not alone,
Other friends may fail me, He is still my own.
Though His hand may lead me over dreary way,
Anywhere with Jesus is a house of praise.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Anywhere! anywhere! Fear I cannot know.
Anywhere with Jesus I can safely go.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Anywhere with Jesus I can go to sleep,
When the darkling shadows round about me creep
Knowing I shall waken never more to roam,
Anywhere with Jesus will be home, sweet home.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Anywhere! anywhere! Fear I cannot know.
Anywhere with Jesus I can safely go.

hymns.title: He leadeth me! O blessed thought
hymns.author: Joseph Henry Gilmore (1834-1918)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: By waters still, o’er troubled sea,
Still ’tis His hand that leadeth me.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: He leadeth me! He leadeth me!
By His own hand He leadeth me;
His faithful follower I would be,
For by His hand He leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, I would clasp Thy hand in mine,
Since it is Thou that leadest me.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: He leadeth me! He leadeth me!
By His own hand He leadeth me;
His faithful follower I would be,
For by His hand He leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: And when my task on earth is done,
When, by Thy grace, the vict’ry’s won,
E’en death’s cold wave I will not flee,
Since Thou in triumph leadest me.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: He leadeth me! He leadeth me!
By His own hand He leadeth me;
His faithful follower I would be,
For by His hand He leadeth me.

hymns.title: I can hear my Savior calling
hymns.author: Ernest W. Blandly

sections.label: Chorus
lines: I'll go [D]with Him, with Him [A7]all the [D]way.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Though the way be dark and dreary,
Though my feet be worn and weary,
Yet my heart keeps bright and cheery
As I follow, follow all the way.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: I will take my cross and follow,
My dear Savior I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
I’ll go with Him, with Him all the way.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And when weak, by grace restore me
As I follow, follow all the way.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: I will take my cross and follow,
My dear Savior I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
I’ll go with Him, with Him all the way.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Through the valley safely lead me,
Every hour, dear Lord, I need Thee
As I follow, follow all the way.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: I will take my cross and follow,
My dear Savior I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
I’ll go with Him, with Him all the way.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: In Thy heart’s affection hold me,
In Thy arms of love enfold me,
And with Thine own grace uphold me,
As I follow, follow all the way.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: I will take my cross and follow,
My dear Savior I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
I’ll go with Him, with Him all the way.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: I would never leave Thee, never;
Nothing from Thy love can sever
As I follow, follow all the way.

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: I will take my cross and follow,
My dear Savior I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
I’ll go with Him, with Him all the way.

hymns.title: Tis so sweet to walk with Jesus
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: ’Tis so safe to walk with Jesus,
Following closely where He leads us,
None can hurt and naught can harm.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Step by step, step by step,
All the day, all the way,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Step by step I’ll walk with Jesus,
Just a moment at a time,
Heights I have not wings to soar to,
Step by step my feet can climb.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Step by step, step by step,
All the day, all the way,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: All the way I’ll walk with Jesus,
Through the sunshine, through the gloom,
Though His blood-marked steps may lead me
To the garden, to the tomb.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Step by step, step by step,
All the day, all the way,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Here a while we walk with Jesus,
But the time will not be long
Till the night shall change to morning,

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Step by step, step by step,
All the day, all the way,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Then, with all who walked with Jesus,
We shall walk with Him in white,
While He turns our grief to gladness,

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: Step by step, step by step,
All the day, all the way,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Step by step, and day by day;
Walking with Thee all the way.

sections.label: Chorus 7
lines: Step by step, step by step,
All the day, all the way,

hymns.title: O blessed life—the heart at rest
hymns.author: William Tidd Matson (1833-1899)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: That [G]trusts a higher will, and deems

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O blessed life, the mind that sees,
Whatever change the years may bring,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O blessed life, as spirit soars,
When sense of mortal sight is dim,
Beyond the sense, beyond to Him,
Whose love unlocks the glorious doors.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O blessed life, heart, mind, and soul,
From self-born aims and wishes free,
In all at one with Deity,
And loyal to the Lord’s control.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O life, how blessed, how divine,
High life, the earnest of a higher;
And let this blessed life be mine.

hymns.title: God in heaven hath a treasure
hymns.author: P. S.; Translated by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)
hymns.lyricist: P. S.; Translated by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: God hath here on earth a [D7]treasure,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: God in tongues of fire descending,
God’s own hand the vessel filling
With the riches of His love.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thus though worn, and tried, and tempted,
Let the Lord but find thee emptied,
Living branch in Christ the Vine!
Vessels weak and poor and base,
Bearing wealth God’s heart is prizing,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh to be but emptier, lowlier,
And to God a vessel holier,
Filled with Christ and Christ alone!
Naught of earth to cloud the glory,
Naught of self the light to dim,
Emptied to be filled with Him.

hymns.title: Lo, from vessels, earthen only
hymns.author: Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Christ, the light that fills the heavens
Light of life ’midst shades of death;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Closing thus His love’s sweet story

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: But the treasure as of old,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: God’s great Gift, His precious Son!

hymns.title: Not I, but Christ be honored, loved, exalted
hymns.author: Mrs. Ada A. Whiddington (1891)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Not I, but [A]Christ be honored, loved, exalt[A7]ed,
[D]Not I, but Christ be [G]seen, be known and [A]heard;
[D]Not I, but [A]Christ in every look and ac[A7]tion,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Oh, to be saved from my[G]self, dear [D]Lord,
[G]Oh, that it may be no more I,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Not I, but Christ to gently soothe in sorrow,
Not I, but Christ to wipe the falling tear;
Not I, but Christ to lift the weary burden,
Not I, but Christ to hush away all fear.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Oh, to be saved from myself, dear Lord,
Oh, to be lost in Thee,
Oh, that it may be no more I,
But Christ that lives in me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ, only Christ, no idle word e’er falling,
Christ, only Christ, no needless bustling sound;
Christ, only Christ, no self-important bearing,
Christ, only Christ, no trace of I be found.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Oh, to be saved from myself, dear Lord,
Oh, to be lost in Thee,
Oh, that it may be no more I,
But Christ that lives in me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Not I, but Christ my every need supplying,
Not I, but Christ my strength and health to be;
Christ, only Christ, for spirit, soul, and body,
Christ, only Christ, live then Thy life in me.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Oh, to be saved from myself, dear Lord,
Oh, to be lost in Thee,
Oh, that it may be no more I,
But Christ that lives in me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ, only Christ, ere long will fill my vision,
Glory excelling soon, full soon I’ll see;
Christ, only Christ, my every wish fulfilling,
Christ, only Christ, my all in all to be.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Oh, to be saved from myself, dear Lord,
Oh, to be lost in Thee,
Oh, that it may be no more I,
But Christ that lives in me.

hymns.title: The earth absorbs the soft, refreshing rain
hymns.author: James Mountain, adapted (1844-1933)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: And [E7]sends it [A]back in flow'rs and [D]fruits again;
So [D7]we re[G]ceive Thy [G7]life so [C]rich and free,
And [A7]live it [G]out for joy and [D7]praise to [G]Thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The moon receives the sun’s bright, golden light,
And gives it forth to cheer the darksome night;
So we receive the rays of light Divine,
And with them on this darkened world we shine.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: ’Tis by Thy love that I can love and bless
The foes who seek to blast my happiness;
Can e’en rejoice, when bearing wrong and shame,
Thou deem’st me meet to suffer for Thy name.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Naught but Thyself can satisfy my heart,
Constrain my will from self and sin to part:
In love so great Thou giv’st Thyself to me;
That I may Thee express eternally.

hymns.title: All I have in Adam is but sin and death
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]All I have in Adam [C]is but sin and [G]death,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When I am in Adam, though I may not sin,
Unto death, a sinner, sentenced I have been;
When in Christ I need not righteously to act,
I’m already righteous, justified in fact.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: In the flesh I need no effort to express
Marks of Adam’s nature and its sinfulness;
In the spirit I need not to strive or strain,
I can live as He is and in spirit reign.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thru my death with Christ, from Adam I am free,
Thru my life with Christ, new life is given me!
Minding not the flesh, old Adam cannot move,
Minding just the spirit, life divine I prove.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Minding just the spirit is God’s saving way,
Minding just the spirit, Christ we will display;
Minding just the spirit, we can overcome,
Minding just the spirit, we the race may run.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Minding just the spirit, we the cross will know,
And His resurrection pow’r thru us will flow;
Minding just the spirit, Christ will live thru me,
And His life within will reach maturity.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: In the spirit Christ is life and all to me,
Living in the spirit, holiness I prove,
And the triune God within my heart doth move.

hymns.title: Christ my very peace is
hymns.author: Witness Lee (1905-1997) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: For the law of life now

hymns.title: There is always something over
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber, adapted (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When we, from the Father’s hand,
Praising for the things He planned.
All our need He doth supply,
When the heart has tasted Jesus
When the heart has tasted Jesus

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: When we share in all His love;
Unplumbed depths still lie beneath us,
We can only praise and wonder
We can only praise and wonder

hymns.title: Mine is the earth, the worlds in all their fulness
hymns.author: Sister Eva of Friedenshort, adapted

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Mine is the spring, when blossoms sweet are blowing,
Wakened from slumb’ring neath the winter snow;
Mine, summer’s wealth, with her bright colors glowing;
Mine is the fruit rich autumn doth bestow.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Mine, all the things created: praise the Giver!
Fish, and all beasts, the birds upon the wing,
Beauty and grace of every living thing.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Mine, all things lovely, blessing every hour,
Wealth of creation, over and around;
Mine is the sun, with its life-giving power,
Mine is the music wonderful of sound.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Mine are the pillars which cannot be shaken—
Truth in the Word, the Word that cannot fall.
Mine is the wisdom which great thoughts awaken
In a man’s soul, that this life is not all.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Knowledge as needed, skill in all the doing,
Mine, when kept closely for my Lord above;
Beauty and wisdom, living streams e’er flowing
Fresh from the springs of God, the God of love.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Mine are the battles, triumph-shouts e’er ringing—
Joy of the warriors for the truth and right;
Mine are the trophies God’s brave ones are bringing,
Heroes of faith and overcoming might.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Mine, mercies granted, and each new awaking,

Yet living on in silent faith.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: The Triune God has now become our all!
This Gift divine we never can exhaust!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: How wonderful, the Son is God’s expression

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: The Triune God has now become our all!

sections.label: Chorus 5

lines: O Will, that willest good alone,

lines: God’s will doth make the bitter sweet,
And all is well when it is done;
Unless His will doth hallow it,
The glory of all joy is gone.

lines: Thy beautiful sweet will, my God,

sections.label: Verse 5

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: It lifts, it bears my happy soul,

My freedom is Thy grand control.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Upon God’s will I lay me down,

No silken couch, nor softest bed,
Could ever give me such deep rest.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Thy wonderful grand will, my God,
With triumph now I make it mine;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Trials give new life to prayer;
Bring me to my Savior’s feet,
Lay me low and keep me there.

lines: Do my heart-strings need Thy stretching,
Do I need for sweetest music
I would yield in full surrender
All Thy heart of love to see.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: In the place of what Thou takest
Thou dost give Thyself to me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I’m ashamed, my Lord, for seeking
Though Thy love has done its stripping,
Yet I’ve been compelled this way.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: In the place of what Thou takest
Thou dost give Thyself to me.

If Thy pleasure means my sorrow,

E’en though Thy delight and glory
Mean that I endure the cross.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: In the place of what Thou takest
Thou dost give Thyself to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Oh, I’ll praise Thee, e’en if weeping
Thou hast made Thyself more precious
Thou increase and I decrease, Lord—

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: In the place of what Thou takest
Thou dost give Thyself to me.

hymns.title: Lord, day by day I view Thy wondrous Cross
hymns.author: B. P. H.

lines: And [D7]day by [G]day I stretch my [C]hands there[G]on

lines: I “glory in the Cross” most loving Lord,
It is the power to save and satisfy,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The daily Cross becomes the deepest joy,
The Cross, I clearly see how Cross and Crown

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh, gracious Lord, how sweet to take from Thee
And know that I can never separate

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: The daily Cross is daily loss to all
The daily Cross is daily gain of all

hymns.title: Via Bethlehem we journey
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber (1869-1930) bio
themes: The Way of Following the Lord
hymns.subcategory: The Way of Following the Lord

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Narrows still as on we go,
Yet God teaches us to know
That the servant is not greater
Than the Lord, who through long years
Hid Himself from this world’s glory,
Follow Him! Count not the tears.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Stones are hurled, and curses hissed
By the men who gather round Him,
Has He not the pathway missed?
And this rough bit of the way
We must travel, since like Jesus,

sections.label: Verse 4

Conflict is but for a day!”

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Then the Cross! for via Calvary
Here we draw the veil, for Jesus
And the memory will have faded
In the glory of His smile!

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Then the grave, with dear ones weeping,
Knowing that all life has fled;
With the men the world calls dead?)
Thence we rise, and live with Jesus,
Throned above the world’s mad strife,
All that worldlings count as life.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: On we press! and yonder gleaming,
The great walls of that fair city,
God has built for such as we;
And we catch the tender music
Of the choirs that sing of One
Who once died to have us with Him
In His kingdom, on the throne.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Just a few more miles, beloved!
And our feet shall ache no more;
No more sin, and no more sorrow,
And I hear Him sweetly whispering,
“Faint not, fear not, still press on,
For it may be ere tomorrow,
The long journey will be done.”

hymns.title: Hast thou no scar

themes: The Way of Following the Lord
hymns.subcategory: The Way of Following the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: I [C]hear thee sung through[F]out the land,

lines: Yet I was wounded by the archers, spent,
Leaned Me against a tree; and rent
By ravening beasts ’round Me, I swooned:
Hast thou no wound? no wound?

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet, as the Master shall the servant be,
And pierced the feet that follow Me;
But whole? can he have followed far
Who has no wound nor scar?

To God are you wholly true?

lines: Do you falter then, or, true to death,

Is filling you day by day?

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: ’Tis the way of the Cross, are you willing for this?
What does bearing the Cross mean to you?
You who’ve given yourself, your all to God!

hymns.title: If I’d know Christ’s risen power

lines: If I’d have Christ formed within me,
I must breathe my final breath,
Put my soul-life e’er to death.

lines: If God thru th’ Eternal Spirit
Nail me ever with the Lord;
Only then as death is working
Will His life thru me be poured.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Gazing thus our sin we see,
Learn Thy love while gazing thus;
Sin which laid the Cross on Thee;
Love which bore the Cross for us.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Here we learn to serve and give,
Here we gather love to live;
Here we gather faith to die.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Captives, by Thy Cross set free;
Soldiers of Thy Cross, we fight.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Still to this our hearts must tend;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Till amid the hosts of light
Through Thy Cross made pure and white,
Cast our crowns before Thy feet.

hymns.title: And wouldst thou live on earth as more than conqu’ror
hymns.author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]And wouldst thou live on earth as [C]"more than [G]conqu'ror"?
Since here a[G]lone the secret [D7]can be [G]found.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He died, and by His death He dealt the death-blow
To sin and Satan’s power for evermore,
And they, who die with Him, shall rise victorious,
And “in this sign” shall triumph more and more.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Cross henceforth their mark of perfect freedom,
What can they lose, who have surrendered all?
What can they fear, who have no reputation?
What shall they shrink from, when His voice doth call?

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: “In this sign,” therefore, go henceforth and conquer,
Finding the place of death the gate of life,
“Life more abundant,” life in all its fulness,
In the deep calm of God, set free from strife.

hymns.title: Cross of Christ! lead onward
hymns.author: Russell Kelso Carter (1849-1928)

hymns.title: Let us contemplate the grape vine
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: But the blossoms of the grape vine
Though they do have some expression,
But a day since they have flowered
Into fruit the blooms have grown;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: To a post the vine is fastened;
To the trellis tied they go.
It can never choose its own way,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: But the master of the vineyard
But with knife and pruning scissors
Then would strip it of its pride.
Caring not the vine is tender,
From the vine are neatly broke.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: In this time of loss and ruin,
Nay, it gives itself more fully
To the one who wounds it so,
To the hand that strips its branches,
That its life may not be wasted,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Leaves are dried and from it drop;
Thus the fruit more richly ripens
Till the harvest of the crop.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Labor of its growth thru suff’ring
Now its fruit is fully ripened,
But the harvest soon is coming,
And its days of comfort flee.

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: Hands will pick and feet will trample
All the riches of the vine,
Till from out the reddened wine-press
Flows a river full of wine.
All the day its flow continues,
Filling all the earth with joy.

sections.label: Verse 10
lines: In appearance now the grape vine
No one offers to repay it
For the cheering wine that’s drunk,
But ’tis stripped and cut e’en further
To a bare and branchless trunk.

sections.label: Verse 11
lines: Yet its wine throughout the winter
Pressed with sorrow, pain, and cares.
Yet without, alone, the grape vine
Midst the ice and snow doth stand,

sections.label: Verse 12

sections.label: Verse 13
lines: As it lifts its arms on high,
And while love doth prune once more,
Strokes it bears as if it never

sections.label: Verse 14
lines: From the branches of the grape vine
Sap and blood and wine doth flow.
Does the vine, for all it suffered,
Drunkards of the earth and wanderers,
From it drink and merry make.

sections.label: Verse 15
lines: Not by gain our life is measured,
But by what we’ve lost ’tis scored;
’Tis not how much wine is drunken,
But how much has been outpoured.
For the strength of love e’er standeth
He who has the greatest suff’ring
Ever has the most to share.

sections.label: Verse 16
lines: Is the best for God to gain;
He who hurts himself most dearly
Most can comfort those in pain.
Has the joys which all surpass.

hymns.title: If it die, oh, hear the message

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Would’st thou see life work in others,
Fall into the ground, be buried,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Dost thou crave to tread the pathway
As thou passest thru death’s gateway

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou shalt learn the blessed secret,

lines: Lord, turn our gaze upon Thy Cross,

Lord, keep our eyes on Calvary.

hymns.title: Death cannot hold the resurrection life

lines: Death cannot hold the resurrection life,
Though all its force against it may combine;
To show the boundless pow’r of life divine.
