hymns.title: Take, drink this cup, His blood
hymns.author: L. K. Q.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Take, drink this cup, each one,
His death show till He come.
Around the table, sup and dine;
We eat the bread and drink the wine.
All blessing in this cup we find.

lines: No blood of cow or goat
Still year by year the same.
A God-man, sinless, He must find
No other offering of His kind,
A spotless lamb for all mankind.

lines: Flows to us, hour by hour.
One sacrifice for all was made,

This cup, our portion blessed of God,

To be en[G]joyed by [D7]man in many [G]ways.

sections.label: Chorus
lines: So all our being [C]sings in praise to [G]Thee,
And Thee we'll eat through [C]all eterni[G]ty;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: O what a shame—when Christ with all His riches,
Has come into the world, life to supply—
That man would live, not by Him, but by teachings,
So powerless these riches to apply.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: But all we need to do is eat the Lord;
And as we eat, we’re inwardly restored;
Christ grows in us, grows to the full.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O Jesus Christ, Thou camest not to mankind
To be a king, to rule us outwardly.
But Thou hast come as food to satisfy us,
And by Thy life to guide us inwardly.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: We praise Thee, Lord, for all Thy glorious grandeur,
For all Thy strength and majesty replete;
And yet, O Lord, what special thanks we give Thee,
That all Thou art is small enough to eat.

hymns.title: Now the Triune God has come to dwell within
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Now the Triune God has [A]come to dwell within
We are mingled [Bm]with the Lord, we're [F♯]one with [Bm]Him

sections.label: Chorus 3

sections.label: Chorus 4

sections.label: Chorus 5

hymns.title: The Spirit today is the air that we breathe
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: For [G]just as our body the [C]breath does re[D]ceive,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The Spirit today is the air that we breathe;
What thing more important than breathing to do?
For breathing each moment, new life we receive,
And God’s living freshness is constant and new.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: For God has been processed, as air now, He’s free;
This life-giving pneuma is all that we need.
He’s rich and abundant, so plentiful, He,
In spirit to walk is to breathe Him indeed.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O, say, aren’t you glad that the Spirit’s outpoured
And God, fully processed, is flowing in us?
So freely we’re breathing this life-giving Lord,

hymns.title: We have come, we have come to the house of God
hymns.author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]We have come, we have come to the house of [Em]God;
We have come [Em7]to the house, [A7]whence outflows the [D]flood.
On the right, day and night, constant is its [G]flow,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: From the house, from the house flows this living stream,
From the house, to the earth, with the life supreme.
Yet more deep, Lord, we seek that the flow may be;
Thus we must be measured and possessed by Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Measure us, measure us, measure every day;
Measure us, measure more, measure all the way,
Till we know that the flow is a mighty flood,
Sweeping over all the earth for Christ the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Take us through, take us through, take us through the flow;
Take us through, through and through, everywhere we go.
Flow increase, never cease, till we swim in Thee,
Till we are immersed in God eternally.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: All shall live, all shall live where the river comes;
All shall live, really live, everywhere it runs.
Let the fount from this mount life abundant bring,
Till the deserts of the earth with churches spring!

sections.label: Chorus 6

lines: This knowledge has developed in the man

So man, created to fulfill God’s plan,
Became a failure full of Satan’s dearth.

lines: Then God came in the Person of the Son;
Lived He on earth, Christ Jesus was His name—
A living model so that everyone
Could live by life, God’s fullness to obtain.

lines: This God-man, Christ, went to the cross and died,
By death He ended knowledge, the old man.
Death He subdued, a new life He began!

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: From death He resurrected and became
The living Spirit to give life to us.
When we believe and call upon His name;
This living Spirit comes to dwell in us.

lines: By this the very Triune God is now
The living Spirit mingling deep within.
Our spirit joins in oneness; this is how
We are one spirit evermore with Him.

We’re now within this Spirit! What a fact!
This Spirit to us all God’s fullness brings!

Each day, each hour, our mind on Him must be;
That by this Spirit we’d be saved within
By life and reign in life eternally.

Thus finishing our God’s eternal plan.

God as our ex[A]perience will the [Bm]wind bring [D]forth;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: There’s a hov’ring cloud a-following the wind,
And the presence of the Lord the cloud does bring,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: God has come to stay with us.
Covering us, the gracious cloud of God—

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: With the cloud continually a fire does flash
It exposes sin, the soul life, and the flesh,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Let it burn! the jealous flame of God;
Let it burn! this all-consuming flame;

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Then from out the fire does the electrum glow,
The redeeming God does our experience show,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Let Him shine! This gold and silver One;
Let Him shine for all to see!
’Tis the Lamb-God who has now become

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Let the wind, cloud, fire and th’ electrum be
Wrought in us, o’er and o’er;
Let this cycle be repeated constantly
More and more, more and more!

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Blow and hover, burn and shine forth, Lord,
That we all may gain Thee constantly

hymns.title: From the north where God is dwelling
hymns.author: Adapted
themes: As the Wind, Cloud, Fire, and Electrum
hymns.subcategory: As the Wind, Cloud, Fire, and Electrum

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: With the cloud we have His presence
In the Lord we put our trust.
But the cloud brings with it fire

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Then from out the flashing fire
God as gold and man as silver
Now are mingled. What a sight!
This bright metal, O Lord Jesus,
O Lord, work Thyself within us
Till th’ electrum in us shines.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: By our passing through this cycle,
To express the life of Jesus;
He with whom we’ve been made one.
We express Him as a human,
As a man so good and fine;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: We express Him as a lion
We express Him as an eagle,
Never held by fear or flatter,
He above it all does fly.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Of the way God deals with us!
From the wind, cloud, fire, electrum,
As the man, the ox and lion,
As we eat Him more and more.

hymns.title: God in His justifying has a plan
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]When we were called, this [G]mighty Lord of [D]all

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: We walked as strangers unaware of Him,
But in His glory God shined deep within,
Infusing His own element in us;
This precious essence was our Lord Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: What glory! How attractive was this light!
How we appreciated such a sight!
Our first reaction was belief in Him—
This precious God has placed Himself within.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Our first reflection of this element
Reflected Jesus back to God, Who sent
His own response to count as righteousness
Our faith in Him Who was infused in us.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: But we would hold to this reality,
Our Jesus Christ in us our all to be,
Content to have this One eternally.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Thus God could never be so satisfied;
Knowing that we cared only to abide
In our experiences of His Son,
Not caring for His goal to make us one.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Still He would seek those faithful saints who’d hear
His call to give up everything so dear,
To offer up their individual Christ;
To come together for the Body life.

hymns.title: God is righteous in His doings
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, how blest the love that spared us,
For the law had judged us dead.
God, to meet the righteous judgment,
Passed it on His Son instead.
Christ, to God has purchased us;

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: God is holy in His nature,
In this way He sanctified us,
Makes our nature one with His.
Making home in all our heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh, how blessed is this process!
It’s our life from day to day.
As we’re minding just the spirit,
Then the mind is life to us,
And the Lord in us is gaining

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: All He is, in full, expressed;
Is the goal which life supplies.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Then the earth will see God’s fullness;
We fore’er will just express Him,
All the sons of God in glory

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Not by running, nor by willing,
Once we were wild olive branches,
Now the root and fat partake,

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: As we’re daily in this process
How we thank Him for the blessing
Of the church life He’s supplied.
Here God is our full enjoyment,
Sons we are, and heirs together,

hymns.title: The cross—we all were there
hymns.author: Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)
themes: All Things Terminated and God Released
hymns.subcategory: All Things Terminated and God Released

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: His life is our rich feast—

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: God has been released in us!

hymns.title: Press on, press on toward the goal
hymns.author: D. M.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [C]Press on, press on toward the goal—
To gain the [G7]prize of [C]God's high call,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Press on, press on, count all things loss.
All that is gain to us,
To win the prize, the Christ of God,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Pressing on! Hallelujah for the prize
We’re pressing on! On and on!
To gain the Christ of God!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Press on, press on to know the Lord
Oh, this is our supreme reward,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Pressing on! Hallelujah for the prize
We’re pressing on! On and on!
To gain the Christ of God!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Press on, press on, this one thing do,
Press onward to the Christ before,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Pressing on! Hallelujah for the prize
We’re pressing on! On and on!
To gain the Christ of God!

hymns.title: There’s a race for us to run—Hallelujah
hymns.author: J. I.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]There's a race for us to [A7]run— Halle[D]lu[G]jah,
And a [D]way for us the [A7]race to [D]win.
To all those who have be[A7]gun— Halle[D]lu[G]jah,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Look away from all the strife and din;
Look away where peace is found—Hallelujah,
Look away from everything to Him.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Look away from everything unto Jesus,
Look away from everything to Him!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Look away from failing self within;
Look away from everything to Him.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Look away from everything unto Jesus,
Look away from everything to Him!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Look away from all the past—Hallelujah,
Look away from both the good and sin;
To the living One hold fast—Hallelujah,
Look away from everything to Him.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Look away from everything unto Jesus,
Look away from everything to Him!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: He who’ll finish what He did begin.
O what grace to run the race—Hallelujah—
We obtain by looking off to Him!

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Look away from everything unto Jesus,
Look away from everything to Him!

hymns.title: There’s a way before us and a race to run
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]There's a way before us and a race to run—
To the [A]law of life with[Bm]in the [D]ark;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: There’s a cloud of witnesses surrounding us,
There is Abel, Enoch, Jacob, Abraham,
John the Baptist greater than them all,
These all died in faith, receiving not

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The Old Testament believers give the call,
For complete perfection they depend on us
We are at the consummation now

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: E’en the least of us is greater than their great.
We’re not small, we’re not small!
They are waiting, watching, and expecting us.
They have run the race and for their sakes
We’ll obey the law of life.
Till the day we’ll all be joined in one

hymns.title: Years I spent in sorrow ’round the cross
hymns.author: F. S.
themes: For Entering the Holy of Holies
hymns.subcategory: For Entering the Holy of Holies

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [C]Years I spent in sorrow 'round the cross,
Then at last the river I did cross,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: [F]Boldly now I come a[C]gain to taste

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In my Christian life I’d daily fall,
Till I left the altar, left it all,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Mercy now is flowing, oh, the grace—
That I find of Him to run the race!
Boldly now I come again to taste

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Brothers, to the Holiest forward come;
Leave your sins behind, the race now run.
Hallelujah! All the work is done—

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Mercy now is flowing, oh, the grace—
That I find of Him to run the race!
Boldly now I come again to taste

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Now within the veil, enjoying God,
Manna, law of life, and budding rod;
Christ Himself, the ark, is our abode—

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Mercy now is flowing, oh, the grace—
That I find of Him to run the race!
Boldly now I come again to taste

hymns.title: Praise God for tidings glad
hymns.author: Adapted
themes: For Entering the Holy of Holies
hymns.subcategory: For Entering the Holy of Holies

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: We're meeting here a[C]round the throne,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: We’re in the veil with God to stay.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: To rise from earth to heav’n,
To be where Christ is now
We’re gathered at the throne of grace,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: As members here in one accord,
We are the Body of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Our spirit now contains all three.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: His ministry is now so fine:
He comes to feed us bread and wine.

hymns.title: Through God’s word, my hope at His returning
hymns.author: Ned Nossaman

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Through God's word, my hope at His re[Em]turning
Yet in times of grief and tribu[Em]lation,
Doubt and [A]fear a[A7]rise, no hope is [D]seen.
In those hours, when prayer cannot be [G]uttered,
Then the Spirit, in like manner, [Em]helps me,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, my prayer is not for deeper suffering,
But that from each trial I’d be free.
Let the cup of bitterness be taken;
Yet, Thy will, not mine, dear Lord, must be.
Even now, though trials sore surround me,
Still within my heart there is a peace,
For the love of God outpoured within me
Floods my heart and bids my doubting cease.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Blest assurance! God has fully ordered
Every matter by His sovereign hand;
Every person (though we see so dimly),
Every thing’s according to His plan.
Every trial is but the Father’s answer
To the groaning of the Spirit’s prayer;
May He gain in every tribulation,
Until we Christ’s glory fully share.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: How could God from all His dealings spare us,
After He spared not His only Son?
Could the Potter’s hand upon the vessel
Ever leave the shaping work undone?
For the center of God’s heart’s desire
Is that many brethren we will be
And to Him, conformed we’ll fully be.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Heirs of God! Joint-heirs with our Lord Jesus!
What a hope of glory this for us!
Though the suff’rings presently seem grievous,
Greater far the glory then for us!
Yea, in all these things we more than conquer,
Through the One whose love has us possessed;
Soon the day for which waits all creation,
When the sons of God are manifest!

hymns.title: Given us, given us, God has given us
hymns.author: Adapted
themes: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
hymns.category: Various Aspects of the Inner Life

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Given us, given us, God has given [Em]us
We believed, we received, now we have all [G]three;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Precious faith in each saint, precious equally,
Precious faith holding us, holding ceaselessly.
Disagree or agree, still it holds us fast,
Day by day, eternally this faith shall last.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Power divine wrought in us is the source so great;
Power divine is in us now to operate.
Hence will spring everything for our life within
And for godliness without, expressing Him.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Promises, promises, all God’s called ones share;
Promises, given us, great and precious are.
These we take to partake of God’s nature true,
Having thus escaped the world’s corruption too.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ within, as the pow’r, in our spirit lives;
Christ without is the Word—all God’s promises.
Now the key is that we daily contact both,
Calling, praying, reading to produce the growth.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Faith and pow’r, promises—these our full supply.
Diligence, diligence, let us now apply;
For if we, to these three, full attention show
From the seed of faith the fruit of love will grow.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: In the growth from the seed many items come;
By this growth in the Lord fruitful we become.
For this we need to see what the Lord’s begun,
Ne’er forgetful be nor blind to what He’s done.

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Diligence day by day will this growth insure;
Diligence thus will make our election sure.
When indeed with this seed we cooperate,
We’re supplied the kingdom’s entrance, rich and great.

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: For this growth, for this growth, Lord, ourselves we give,
By the faith, promises, and the pow’r to live.
Nothing more, nothing less, will our basis be
By Thy grace we will cooperate with Thee.

hymns.title: The Lord of all has shown His plan
hymns.author: B. B. P.; B. P.
themes: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
hymns.category: Various Aspects of the Inner Life

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]The Lord of all has [A]shown His plan
To be His Bride we [A]must match Him,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Like virgins who so single are,
They love the Groom so much,
They in His presence ever stay—
Lord, make us those who are so wise,
The wise ones who enjoy the feast,
Who all the price will pay.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The virgins are mature in life,
They daily eat and drink the Lord,
Our need today is growth in life,
Not knowledge, teachings, gifts, nor pow’r—
But life is all we need.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord, as the seed of life within,
Grow more in us each day;
By spreading from our deepest part,
Lord, strengthen Thou our inner man;
Make home in all our heart.

hymns.title: If from your nat’ral man you would be free
hymns.author: Unknown
themes: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
hymns.category: Various Aspects of the Inner Life

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]If from your nat'ral man you would be free,
This law trans[D7]forms us, [G]to Christ conforms us—

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: From life divine it does originate,
Its function, working, power are innate,
Stop all your trying, on life relying,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: The law of life fulfills our God’s desire,
Our self-improvement He does not require,
God’s plan fulfilling; Yes, Lord, we’re willing,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Old man denying, God’s life supplying,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: This law’s inscribing Christ upon our hearts,
’Til He is written in our inward parts,
Christ’s form engraving, not mere behaving,

hymns.title: Dig away, dig away, dig away
hymns.author: R. K.
themes: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
hymns.category: Various Aspects of the Inner Life

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Dig away, dig a[D]way, dig a[G]way,

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Dig a[G]way, dig a[D]way, dig a[G]way,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All my vain imaginations dig away!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All my vain imaginations dig away!

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: All my dreams have to go
That His life may flow... Hallelujah!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All my vain imaginations dig away!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All my troublesome emotions dig away!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All my troublesome emotions dig away!

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: All self love has to go
That His life may flow... Hallelujah!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All my troublesome emotions dig away!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All resistance in my will dig away!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All resistance in my will dig away!

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: All self will has to go
That His life may flow... Hallelujah!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All resistance in my will dig away!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All self seeking in my heart dig away!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All self seeking in my heart dig away!

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: All my hopes have to go
That His life may flow... Hallelujah!
Dig away, dig away, dig away,
All self seeking in my heart dig away!

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Life can flow, praise the Lord, life can flow!
From the fountain in my heart life can flow!
Life can flow, praise the Lord, life can flow!
From the fountain in my heart life can flow!

sections.label: Chorus 6
lines: Christ can flow through me... Hallelujah!
Life can flow, praise the Lord, life can flow!
From the fountain in my heart life can flow!

hymns.title: God has not giv’n us a spirit of fear
hymns.author: Adapted
themes: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
hymns.category: Various Aspects of the Inner Life

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [A]God has not giv'n us a [D]spirit of [A]fear—
We have His Word— brothers, [D]sisters, let's [A]hear—

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: God has not giv’n us a wavering will—
There’s pow’r deep within, pow’r deep within!
But one our spirit will strengthen and fill—

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: O there’s pow’r, pow’r, overcoming pow’r,
O there’s pow’r, pow’r, normal Christian pow’r
In the spirit God’s given us!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: God has not giv’n us emotions so weak—
There’s pow’r deep within, pow’r deep within!
Open our hearts and in love let us speak—

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: O there’s pow’r, pow’r, overcoming pow’r,
O there’s pow’r, pow’r, normal Christian pow’r
In the spirit God’s given us!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: God has not giv’n us a mind that is bound—
There’s pow’r deep within, pow’r deep within!
But one that’s healthy and perfectly sound—

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: O there’s pow’r, pow’r, overcoming pow’r,
O there’s pow’r, pow’r, normal Christian pow’r
In the spirit God’s given us!

hymns.title: We have an inner life; that’s for our daily life
hymns.author: B. F.; G. C.; J. F.
hymns.lyricist: B. F.; G. C.; J. F.
themes: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
Inner Life, Daily Life, Meeting Life
hymns.category: Various Aspects of the Inner Life
hymns.subcategory: Inner Life, Daily Life, Meeting Life

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]We have an [Bm]inner life; [Em]that's for our [A7]daily life;
[D]We'll live the inner life; [G]we'll have the [A7]daily life;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Christ is our inner life; He’s in our spirit now;
Not far away from us—He’s right inside!
And as we turn to Him and take Him as our all
He will become in us our inner life.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Out from our inner life will come our daily life,
And all our living be filled up with Christ.
Then as we live by Him, He lives His life in us,
And He becomes to us our daily life.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: The real experience of Christ in daily life,
Will fill the meeting life with Christ Himself.
Not empty forms and such, but Christ will be so much;
And we will see Him here as the meeting life.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Without the inner life there is no daily life,
There is no meeting life, there is no church!
Christ as our inner life, Christ in our daily life
Will make the meeting life new and glorious!

hymns.title: Lord, we’ve heard the call, Come forward
hymns.author: D. P.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: We come forward by a new way,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: We come forward unto our God,
Who is sitting on the throne;
He has paved the way to glory
By His blood and cross alone.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: We come forward to the new age,
With assured heart, true and bold.
Ne’er to shrink back to the old.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Praise You, Lord, we’ve all come forward.
You’re our God and we’re Your people;

hymns.title: If from the world you’re longing to be free
hymns.author: Adapted from Henry Godden Jackson (1838-1914)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]If from the world you're longing to be free,
[D]If you would live in all reality,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: If with your sin and self you would be through,
If you would let the Lord your mind renew,
His Word is living, life-power giving—

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ as the land of Canaan is our lot—
If you would enter, harden not your heart—
His Word discerns us, all that concerns us—

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus is coming, now He’s on His way—
Would you be ready if He comes today—
His Word prepares us, to Jesus bears us—

hymns.title: What a wonderful change in my living is wrought
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]What a wonderful change in my living is [G7]wrought
More of Christ into me at each instance is brought

sections.label: Chorus
lines: Thus the Lord takes my heart, and transforms every part,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: What I never could do God is doing in me,
By saying Amen to His Word.
And the change is so real all the brothers can see,
By saying Amen to God’s Word.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I have ceased from my wandering and going astray
By saying Amen to God’s Word.
And my old inclinations are passing away
By saying Amen to His Word.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Now the secret of faith in the Lord I can see—
It’s saying Amen to His Word.
He is more real and precious than all things to me
By saying Amen to His Word.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Now my love for the brothers abounds more and more
By saying Amen to God’s Word.
And I’m being related as never before
By saying Amen to His Word.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Now my hope in the Lord’s soon return groweth bright
By saying Amen to His Word.
I am ready to see Him, my Lord, my delight,
By saying Amen to His Word.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Lord Jesus, Amen to Your Word,
Lord Jesus, Amen to Your Word.
You are coming again—all my heart says Amen!
Lord Jesus, Amen to Your Word!

hymns.title: Remove the veils, Lord, from my heart
hymns.author: R. K.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The power that raised Christ from the dead;
When I by faith this power receive,
I to the church am led.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy mighty power has set me free
From all the world’s distracting things;
An entrance to the local church

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Once in the local church, I need
To take Thee as my person, Lord;
My outward man each day recede,
My heart is for the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: I take Thee as my person, Lord;
I have been crucified with Thee.
My inner man has been restored;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: When all Thy members self forsake,
Thy glorious Body, Lord, is known;
When of Thy Person we partake,
The one new man is shown.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: The church life is the one new man
Thy Body is a corporate man,

hymns.title: Jesus, our wonderful Shepherd
hymns.author: Adapted

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In the divisions He sought us,
Into the good land He brought us,
Oh, to our spirit how good!

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Feasting from such a rich store!
Here where we’re dwelling in oneness

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He is the food that we eat;
We as His sheep are fed richly

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Feasting from such a rich store!
Here where we’re dwelling in oneness

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Dwell we here on a high mountain,
Slaking our thirst at the fountain,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Feasting from such a rich store!
Here where we’re dwelling in oneness

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ is our rest and enjoyment,
Here we have nothing to fear;
Here all the sheep dwell securely,
Kept by His presence so dear.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Feasting from such a rich store!
Here where we’re dwelling in oneness

hymns.title: Sing aloud your praises to the Lord of all
hymns.author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [Dm]Sing aloud your praises [Gm]to the Lord of [Dm]all,
Tell among us all His [Gm]doings great and [Dm]small,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: In the Holy City with His own He dwells;
O Lord, our Lord, how excellent Thy name!
He’s enthroned upon the praises of His saints;
All His delight in Zion does remain.
The local churches are His move today—
He is our portion, we are satisfied.
Oh, what a goodly heritage have we;
Oh, what a goodly heritage have we!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Who shall in His holy tabernacle dwell,
Who shall ascend to His most holy hill?
Those who seek for Him and purify their heart;
This generation now that seeks His face.
Oh, seek His face, ye children of the earth,
Open your heart, and let the King come in.
He will come in, and He shall live and reign;
He will come in, and He shall live and reign!

lines: [A7]Jesus [D]is my King all- glorious, so [G]wide, so deep His [D]love;

Later called the Naza[A7]rene from Gali[D]lee.
[D7]For [G]thirty- three years serving, de[D]spised, refused by men,
[A7]Healing, [D]teaching, suffering hunger, no [G]bed His aches to [D]cheer,
So immense, so wonder[A7]ful a love is [D]this.

lines: He, my King, my Lord, my Savior, my welling Fount of love,
Walked the lonely path to dark Gethsemane.
Sweat like blood-drops for my peril, obeyed His Father’s will,
Paid the price to save all men eternally.
Despised, man’s insult’s taking, the sinner’s blame endured,
Bore the cross unto Golgotha willingly,
Scarred by nails and scarred by spear, whence blood and water streamed,
So immense His love expressed to full degree.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus is my King of mercy, with love immeasurable;
On the cross He prayed, and mercy’s heart was shown.
There a dying thief repented, received salvation’s word;
Jesus bore all sins, rejected, left alone.
What piercing pain and sorrow, with vinegar and gall,
Unto God He did depart victorious,
Resurrected and ascended, our interceding Christ,
He reveals His love so deep and wonderous.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus is my King victorious; His love my heart has touched.
For this sinner He has died, His love to show.
I am healed and cleansed completely, and in His mercies rest,
Taught by Him and guided, on His path I go.
Temptations fierce unheeding, salvation is my wall;
I’m empowered daily as I go along.
With eyes on Him in glory, I sing with heart renewed,
And His love is all the message of my song.

hymns.title: In A Lifetime Never Met A Clever Rival
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: It seems one comes to rob my home;
I fear my final day has come—
With every ounce of strength, resist.
He comes to wrestle; I defend:
I’ll fight Him to the bitter end.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: How strange! Though every wile I’ve used,
For one whole night, yet still He stands.
I see my strength has been reduced,
And yet revenge is not His plan.
How strange! Although I can’t get free,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I’ve never met with such a foe,
And even if He states His name,
Of this opponent naught I know,
But that from Him reward I’d gain.
I’d force Him blessing to bestow,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: ’Tis dawn, yet have I won, or He?
My Rival, forced, now blesses me,
But when I rise, my thigh is lame.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: The faintest light in darkened heart
If I’m so strong, why grasp the heel?
If victor, why the crippled thigh?
’Twas He who won and left this sign,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: A flood of light: This heart of mine,
As breaks the dike by swelling tide,
Must worship, and in shame must hide.
So great my sin, I must confess:

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: That these, mine own two hands, rebelled
The mighty God to stop and held!

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: Thou, God, dost shine so gloriously;
Thou, Lord of hosts, resplendent, bright,
I must repent and bow the knee.

sections.label: Verse 10
lines: How can it be that I could see
Him face to face and hand to hand?
If only earth would swallow me,
My shame to hide, my life to end.
Why did I not, at life’s first start,
Pass on, from earth in sleep depart?

sections.label: Verse 11
lines: I hate myself; my heart was dim,
For blinded were mine eyes by pride;
Now, at the thought of conquering Him,
Not just my thigh, but all my strength

sections.label: Verse 12
lines: As I look back at all my life,
I see that it’s corrupt entire.
For self, my God I sacrificed;
My foolish heart knew but desire.
What then I thought that “blessing” be
Was forcing God to grant my plea.

sections.label: Verse 13
lines: “I wish: the heav’n must fall in line.
I plan: my Lord must coincide.
I want: my God should step aside.
I work: my God must be my guide.
When I am rushed, He must not stay,
For once, His victory to display.”

sections.label: Verse 14
lines: There’s one so evil here below,
Lord, that I’m Jacob Thou dost know:
One Thou should’st but detest and hate;
No hope have I but mercy Thine
Upon this wretched heart of mine.

sections.label: Verse 15
lines: I grope — at once His mercy find.
At first lame step — His grace is mine!
If I forget, my wounded thigh
Reminds: on naught can I rely.
Though Israel I’m named by Thee,
Yet Jacob ever lame shall be.

sections.label: Verse 16
lines: In Thy defeat, defeat I’d claim;
To Thee I yield my victory;
Thy weakness drops me to my knees.
In fear and trembling all my days
Thy will I’d do, Thy name I’d praise.

hymns.title: Unclean Lips, Impure Heart
hymns.author: Translated from Watchman Nee (1903-1972)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: My lips are foul, my heart impure;
All my past hopes no more endure;
Lord, hast Thou yet some grace for me?

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When humble, I on self rely;
E’en the remorseful tears I shed,
These, too, Thy cleansing blood require.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: My heart is my own enemy;
Lord, may my hope yet in Thee stay?

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: I dare not stop, nor can I work;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: The old creation’s hard to shed;
If I but move, there self is mired.
Oh, that Thy glory Thou wouldst send,
My heart to flood and bless entire.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Naught dare I ask, nor aught avow;
Naught can I do but gaze on Thee.
Might Thou Thy precious Word bestow,

hymns.title: When I Receive Gifts, I Can Give Grace
hymns.author: Translated from Watchman Nee (1903-1972)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: All of my life’s been filled with woes,
Trials beyond what most could bear;
Though of my suff’rings no one knows,
Yet of my staunchness I’m aware;
I think self’s been discarded, yet
What I’ve been through, I don’t forget!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I have received much grace, I know;
No one on earth more so than I!
Upon my body, in my soul,
Evidence of God’s work I find.
I know all He has done in me,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: All my success I clearly see,
And know my every righteous deed;
My center shifts from God to me;

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: When friends console me in my plight,
I can no more conceal my pride,
I fail as any common folks:
Cursing my birth, I’m thus exposed.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: O God, about Thee, much I’ve heard,
And can expound on Thee at length,
Yet my poor self’s corrupt, impure;
Never have I for Thee been changed;
I use Thy gifts to pride inflate,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: But now mine eye has seen Thee, Lord;
Thy shining light — I am destroyed,
I hate myself; How could I be

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Oh, how ashamed, ashamed am I!
Self I adorned with Thy free grace!
I used Thy works to lift self high;
My every motive’s low and base;

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: What shame, that I so proud can be!
Thy glory stealing for my self.

sections.label: Verse 10
lines: That I’m corrupt, Thou knowest well;
As for myself, I had no clue;
I thought I could rely on self,
But it is shameful, through and through;
O Lord, today, please rescue me!
Come loose my bonds, and set me free!

sections.label: Verse 11
lines: O Lord, my heart doth Thee implore:
Grant me some dust in which to lie;
Ashes to on my body pour,
That so corrupt my heart could be.

sections.label: Verse 12
lines: My life is shallow to the core;
And all my being I abhor.
I hate myself now, O my Lord;
My only hope: abide in Thee.

sections.label: Chorus 4

hymns.title: Though we are often swayed and tossed
hymns.author: Adapted from Annie Johnson Flint (1866-1932); Unknown, vv. 5-7

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Our heart may be changing often,
But our need He won’t forsake.
Though we spurn Him, still He loves us;
Worldly friends our hearts would break.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All that we to Him would trust.
To the uttermost He loves us,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Grieve His heart, His love forget,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: He to whom we’ve been ungrateful

sections.label: Verse 4

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Things of earth will soon be gone;
Why let them rule my soul?
Once I watched for His return;

sections.label: Verse 6

This foul place I then must leave,
Now regain my long lost love,

lines: Lord, I believe, Lord, I believe!
Savior, raise my faith in Thee,

hymns.title: Lord Jesus, Lord Jesus! Why Dost Thou Not Come?
hymns.author: Translated from Watchman Nee (1903-1972)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [C]Jesus, Lord! Jesus, Lord! [Dm]Why dost Thou not [G7]come?
They all hope; [G]we al[F]so for Thy [G]coming [F]sigh.
[C]Earth and space age apace, [Dm]yet all wait for [G]Thee;

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus Lord, Jesus Lord! Why dost Thou delay?
What prevents Thine advent? Why not come today?
Generations of saints waited all their lives;
We’ve watched here, tens of years, for Thee to arrive.
Why not please cut short these lengthy yearning days?
O Lord, heed this our plea: Come without delay.
Come without delay. Come without delay.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus, Lord! Jesus, Lord! Why dost Thou not come?
Since Thou went into heav’n, nothing here I love,
Days below seem as though there’s no break of dawn;
On my face, seems no trace of a joy long gone.
Passion, drive, once alive, no more in me burn;
Jesus Lord! Jesus Lord! Why don’t You return?
Why don’t You return? Why don’t You return?

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Please come back! Please come back! All around I see
Some grow slack, some slide back, some change gradually;
Love once bold groweth cold, suff’ring takes its toll;
Faith and sighs mingled rise, forward steps are slowed;
Lamp of hope dimmer grows, can’t hold out much more.
Seeing these, come back, please! Why still tarry, Lord?
Why still tarry, Lord? Why still tarry, Lord?

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus, Lord! Jesus, Lord! Why art Thou not here?
Jesus, Lord! Jesus, Lord! Why dost not appear?
Till what date must I wait? Till what year, what day?
As I stay, watch and pray, patience ebbs away;
Jesus, Lord! Jesus, Lord! Quickly come, I pray!
Jesus, Lord! Jesus, Lord! Quickly come, I pray!
Quickly come, I pray! Quickly come, I pray!

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Sometimes there's [A]clear blue [D]sky, but clouds most [G]of the [A]time;
Some[G]times I [A]find a sweet [F♯m]song in the [Bm]night; more [Em]often, [A7]there's no [D]rhyme;
For [G]I'm compelled then to [F♯m]seek out God's [Bm]will and [Em]His de[A7]light.
To [D]what hot [A]blaze must Thy [Bm]fire be [D]raised till [G]trials [A]are com[D7]plete?
How [G]deep, how [A7]painfully [F♯m]must Thy thorn [Bm]pierce, till [G]there's an [A7]outflow [D]sweet?

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Sometimes a thorn must pierce, Thy pow’r to manifest;
At times I have wandered, near death and loss, no food, no home, no rest.
Sometimes I need to lose all that I have, to fully be set free;
When penniless, I don’t beg, having faith, not anxiety.
Sometimes there’s fighting too, between the brothers dear,
Each wants to score the most powerful blow, rage everywhere;
Refusing visitors, sing I to Thee, whose heart’s most pained by these;
My loss with Thine can’t compare, but I’d learn to share Thy sufferings.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I’ve reached the end of life, my fleeting years passed by;
Here in Thy presence, I hear time “tick” by, I feel the dusk draw nigh;
The winter moon is beginning to wane; my life, too, ebbs away,
Ahead, not many dark clouds yet remain, most lie behind;
My future draws a line, which from my past divides,
With each day’s passing, the conflicts of life are all untied;
As light from “visible” fadeth from sight, “invisible” is seen;
My hope is set on that hope in the heav’ns, with it my heart shall be.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My days have turned to months, my months have turned to years,
Years into a lifetime that waxes and wanes, and soon the end appears;
In retrospect, which of these is most sweet? Sunrise, or set of sun?
’Tis set of sun, for it’s nearer to Thee, to Thy dear home!
Awaiting Thy return, my heart is weary, spent,
My eyes are dimming, and soon I’ll depart from this life’s tent;
The mountains smile as they call me to rest, my burdens to unload;
Now ev’ry weight has been melted away. I go, I quickly go!

sections.label: Chorus 10

Nothing between us but fellowship dear.
Hidden in Christ, under grace o’er us spanned.

Four living creatures whose wings meet as one,
Wings straight, and covering, wings paired on each side,
Pointing to Christ, worthy, pure, dignified.

lines: In Christ we speak, this Your oracle grants.
Heaven is open! Our skies are so clear,
Stretched forth like crystal, both awesome and sheer.

lines: We are Your people, You’re our God.
In us do rule and reign.
You are the man upon the throne
God planned and willed that You be Head,
The Lord of all made known.

lines: Those God foreknew, He set apart
That You would be His firstborn Son
You conquered death and rose with might
You carry out God’s will on earth,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: You, as God’s heir, uphold all things.
You make God’s substance known by all
As from Your throne life springs.

sections.label: Verse 5

You take the lead, we follow You.
And seat us there with You.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Under the ruling of Your life,
We too will reign as kings,
Your rule is all we need.

All that You are is our bequest.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]Like Christ, who sought us, brought us to His [A]keep,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Tend to His sheep and care for all their needs!
Bring God’s supply, which out of love proceeds!
Reach those whose burdens seem too much to bear!
Nurture their heart and soul through loving care!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Our Father’s care meets every inward need,
Binds all our wounds till we are buoyant, freed.
His tender love heals broken, wounded hearts,
Restores communion and His life imparts.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Day after day, by taking in the Word,
Proof God is caring for us tenderly.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Have we not found green pastures, there to lay,
Waters of rest, with paths to mark our way?
Led through the valley, guided inwardly,
Come to the Father’s presence joyfully!

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Christ as our joy protects us from attacks!
We shelter in His presence hour by hour!

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: God’s heart toward us is good in every way.
Are we His match in all we do and say,
Stewards, whose hearts the love of Christ constrains,
Who minister the food that builds the saints?

sections.label: Verse 8
lines: Shepherding needs the maintenance of life,
The cross annulling selfishness and strife,
Prayers full of light that set our hearts ablaze,
Till every word we speak God’s love conveys!

sections.label: Verse 9
lines: Treasure the saints! Each one is such a gift!
Obey our King to mend each inward rift!
Honor the Body, holding to the Head,
His covenant of peace the way we’re led!

sections.label: Verse 10
lines: Our words and actions are the gateway in;
Live Christ by speaking, building to begin!
Shoulder the lost and rescue the forlorn!
Stitch upon stitch, our wedding gown adorn.

sections.label: Verse 11
lines: The flock is cared for, cherished in this way!
The Father loves us as He loves the Son,
His love the bond that joins us all as one!

I [D]hold You as my Head today.

I ask You to shepherd my soul.
I give You my heart as a whole.

As, choice after choice, I seek You,
In me You establish Your throne.
I open to let my King in,
Nor will I resist You, but still
I raise the white flag of defeat,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Your cross is my gateway to joy.
Your heart toward me harbors the best.
I love You with all of my heart.
For me, You are second to none.
The cross has turned everything sweet;
I find my delight in the Son!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: I live for Your sake, not my own.

Lord, You are the One seated there.
We all are enjoying Your reign.
The church is Your Kingdom on earth,

sections.label: Verse 6

hymns.title: The Cross is Not a Suffering
hymns.author: L. S.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]The way of consecration is an [C]exercise to[G]day
To stay in spirit, faithfully, de[A7]nying self this [D]way.
The [G]choice of source remains before us [C]every day to [G]choose
Be[C]tween the soul and spirit, death and [D]life, to [D7]gain or [G]lose.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: The Christ we know is crucified — experience of the cross
Allows us to enjoy His life and count ourselves but loss;
The sense of life and death within us functions as a gauge,
Equipping us to live Christ in the Body in this age.
To deepen and increase our joy
In Christ, His way to trace.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Draw closer to the Lord and drink the river of supply,
With every choice and turn allowing Christ to occupy
Our heart in all its inward parts, as open as can be,
Maintaining our enjoyment of the Lord continually.
Of all we are, the end,
But Christ, with God to blend.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: God’s glory in the face of Christ, His presence inwardly,
Compels us to deny the self and follow faithfully;
As deep as His restrictions go, the riverbed is laid,
For that’s how deep the river flows, God’s life to us conveyed.
The cross is but a threshold
For life to flow within us deeply,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: The churches are the house of God. His presence limits us.
He’s standing at the gate and holds a reed to measure thus —
Examining and testing, He is judging to possess
Our inward being by the living flow that swallows death.
The cross brings in the river
That flows out from the house
Like the Bride to her espoused.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: “The marriage of the Lamb has come,” will soon be heard by all,
“His wife made herself ready,” proving naught can life forestall.
Around the bend, the Lord will come and gather up His saints,
Those ready for His coming, loving Him without constraints.
The cross is truly God’s way;
The way that we go on!

lines: [G]Would of Thy [D]love in all its [Bm]breadth and length,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: It passeth telling, that dear love of Thine,
My Savior, Jesus; yet these lips of mine
Would fain proclaim to sinners, far and near,
A love which can remove all guilty fear,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: It passeth praises, that dear love of Thine,
My Savior, Jesus; yet this heart of mine
Would sing that love, so full, so rich, so free,
Which brings a rebel sinner, such as me,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: But though I cannot sing, or tell, or know
The fulness of Thy love, while here below,
My empty vessel I may freely bring;
O Thou, who art of love the living spring,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: I am an empty vessel—not one thought
Or look of love to Thee I’ve ever brought;
Yet I may come, and come again to Thee,
With this the empty sinner’s only plea,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Oh, fill me, Jesus, Savior, with Thy love!
Lead, lead me to the living fount above;
Thither may I, in simple faith draw nigh,
And never to another fountain fly,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Lord Jesus, when Thee face to face I see,
When on Thy lofty throne I sit with Thee,
Then of Thy love, in all its breadth and length,
Its height and depth, its everlasting strength,

hymns.title: I have a Friend, whose faithful love
hymns.author: C. A. Tydeman

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He held the highest place above,
Adored by all the sons of flame,
He laid aside His crown and came
Of heavenly rank and earthly fame
He sought me—Blessed be His name!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: It was a lonely path He trod,
Known only to Himself and God
Was all the grief that filled His heart,
Till where I lay in want and shame,
He found me—Blessed be His name!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Then dawned at last that day of dread,
With wearied frame and thorn-crowned head,
And, dying there in grief and shame,
He saved me—Blessed be His name!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Long as I live my song shall tell
The wonders of His dying love;
And when at last I go to dwell
With Him His sovereign grace to prove,
And bowing there with loud acclaim
I’ll praise Him—Blessed be His name!

hymns.title: My song shall be of Jesus
hymns.author: Fanny Crosby (1820-1915)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: My song shall be of Jesus
And when my soul shall enter
A song of praise to Jesus

sections.label: Chorus 2

I call to mind His goodness
My song shall be of Jesus,
I’ll sing the grace that saves me,
And keeps me at His side.
I’ll sing the grace that saves me,
And keeps me at His side.

My heart is filled with ecstasy,
As in Thy face of radiancy

I do not wish to go out free,
To serve Thee to the end.

lines: I cannot sing enough of Thee,
A note so full of melody
Comes from my heart so joyously,

hymns.title: Gathered in Thy name, Lord Jesus
hymns.author: C. A. W.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Loved with love which knows no measure,
Save the Father’s love to Thee,
Blessed Lord, our hearts would treasure
All the Father’s thoughts of Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: All His joy, His rest, His pleasure—
All His deep delight in Thee—
Lord, Thy heart alone can measure
What Thy Father found in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: How He set His love upon Thee—
Yet for us He did not spare Thee,
By Thy death our life was won.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O the joy, the wondrous singing,
When we see Thee as Thou art!
Thy blest name, Lord Jesus, bringing

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Through God’s endless day of days.

hymns.title: Jesus, Thou Joy of loving hearts
hymns.author: Bernard of Clairvaux (1090-1153) bio; Translated by Ray Palmer (1808-1887)
hymns.lyricist: Bernard of Clairvaux (1090-1153) bio; Translated by Ray Palmer (1808-1887)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, Thou Joy of loving hearts,
Thou Fount of life, Thou Light of men,
From the best bliss that earth imparts,
We turn unfilled to Thee again.
Thy truth unchanged hath ever stood;
Thou savest those that on Thee call;
To them that seek Thee, Thou art good,
To them that find Thee, all in all!

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: We taste Thee, O Thou living Bread,
And long to feast upon Thee still;
We drink of Thee, the Fountain-head,
And thirst our souls from Thee to fill!
Our restless spirits yearn for Thee,
Where’er our changeful lot is cast;
Glad when Thy gracious smile we see,
Blest, when our faith can hold Thee fast.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O Lord, be Thou our strength and stay!
Make all our moments calm and bright,
Chase all dark thoughts of sin away,
Shed o’er us here Thy holy light.

hymns.title: O Jesus, Jesus, dearest Lord
hymns.author: Frederick William Faber (1814-1863); Chorus by Russell Kelso Carter (1849-1928)
hymns.lyricist: Frederick William Faber (1814-1863); Chorus by Russell Kelso Carter (1849-1928)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I love Thee so I know not how
Thy love is like a burning fire

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: O Jesus, Lord, with me abide;
I rest in Thee, whate’er betide;
Thy gracious smile is my reward;
I love, I love Thee, Lord!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: For Thou to me art all in all;
My heart’s desire, my body’s strength,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: O Jesus, Lord, with me abide;
I rest in Thee, whate’er betide;
Thy gracious smile is my reward;
I love, I love Thee, Lord!

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Burn, burn, O love, within my heart,
Till all the dross of earthly loves

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: O Jesus, Lord, with me abide;
I rest in Thee, whate’er betide;
Thy gracious smile is my reward;
I love, I love Thee, Lord!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O light in darkness, joy in grief,
Jesus, my love, my treasure, who
Can tell what Thou art worth?

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: O Jesus, Lord, with me abide;
I rest in Thee, whate’er betide;
Thy gracious smile is my reward;
I love, I love Thee, Lord!

Thy flight, where wilt Thou stay?
On, on! our Lord is sweeter far

sections.label: Chorus 6

I rest in Thee, whate’er betide;

I love, I love Thee, Lord!

hymns.title: On the table of Thy love
hymns.author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: ’Tis the blood Thou shedd’st for us,
That our sins may be forgiv’n;
That Thy blessings may be giv’n.
Thou didst drink the cup of wrath,
Thou hast tasted death for us,
Thus the cup of blessing bought,
As the portion gained for us.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: In this portion we have God,
Whom we lost thru Adam’s fall;
By the shedding of Thy blood,
God becomes our all in all.
In this portion all we have—
All that God has planned and willed,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: In this cup of God’s design.
Here in love we drink this cup

hymns.title: Rivers of living water
hymns.author: G. R. H. Wood

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Send now this life through me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Cleanse me, oh, cleanse me, my Savior,
Empty me, fill me and use me,
Teach me to trust and obey.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Send now this life through me.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Then, and then only, Lord Jesus,
Through me the rivers can flow;
Thus and thus only will others
Learn Thy great fulness to know.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Send now this life through me.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Here I lay all at His feet;
Just for His service made meet!

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Send now this life through me.

hymns.title: Thou Breath from still eternity
hymns.author: Gerhard Tersteegen (1697-1769); Translated by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)
hymns.lyricist: Gerhard Tersteegen (1697-1769); Translated by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1827-1909)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: May I in will and deed and word
Obey Thee as a little child;
And keep me in Thy love, my Lord,
Within me teach, and strive, and pray,
Lest I should choose my own wild way.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy Spirit, Stream by Thee, the Son,
Is opened to us crystal pure,
Forth flowing from the heavenly throne
To waiting hearts and spirits poor;
Athirst and weary do I sink
Beside Thy waters, there to drink.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My spirit turns to Thee and clings,
Thy living Stream, Thy gracious Rain,
None wait for these, and wait in vain.

hymns.title: Lord, the Spirit, Truth divine
hymns.author: Samuel Longfellow (1819-1892)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Dawn upon this heart of mine;
Word of God, and inward light,
Wake my spirit, clear my sight.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Glow within this heart of mine,
Perish self in Thy pure fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Fill and nerve this will of mine;
By Thee may I strongly live,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Still this restless heart of mine,
Speak to calm this tossing sea,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Gladden Thou this heart of mine;
In the desert ways I’ll sing:

hymns.title: Loved with everlasting love
hymns.author: George Wade Robinson (1838-1877)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Since I know, as now I know,
I am His, and He is mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Things that once were wild alarms
Doubt and care and self resign,
While He whispers in my ear,
I am His, and He is mine.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Who the Lord and me shall part?
Ah, with what a rest of bliss
Christ can fill the loving heart.
Heaven and earth may fade and flee,
But, while God and I shall be,
I am His, and He is mine.

hymns.title: Come and rejoice with me
hymns.author: Elizabeth Rundle Charles (1828-1896)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I, once so sick at heart,
Have met with One who knows my case,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: And I have found a mighty arm

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: My feet so wide did roam,
And One has brought me from afar,
To find in Him my home.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: For I have found a Friend
Who knows my heart’s most secret depths,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: I knew not of His love;
And He had loved so long,
With love so faithful and so deep,

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: And now I know it all,
Have heard and known His voice,
And hear it still from day to day.

hymns.title: Jesus, Jesus, Jesus
hymns.author: A. Paget Wilkes

hymns.title: Cleansed in our Savior’s precious blood
hymns.author: William Spencer Walton

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Leaning our heads on Jesus’ breast,
Knowing the joy of that sweet rest,
Finding in Him the chief, the best,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Kept by His pow’r from day to day,
Held by His hand, we cannot stray,
Glory to glory all the way,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Living in us His own pure life,
Giving us rest from inward strife,
From strength to strength, from death to life,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: O what a Savior we have found;
Well may we make the world resound

hymns.title: Full salvation! Full salvation
hymns.author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh, the rapturous bliss to know.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thought, and wish, and senses keeping
From the guilt and power of sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Lo! my heart the Spirit’s shrine:
God and man in oneness blending,
Raised in Christ to life divine!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Care and doubting, gloom and sorrow,
Fear and shame are mine no more;
Faith knows naught of dark tomorrow,

Stoop down, and drink, and live.”
I came to Jesus, and I drank
My thirst was quenched, my soul revived,
And now I live in Him.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say,
Look unto Me, thy morn shall rise,
And all thy day be bright.”
I looked to Jesus, and I found
In Him my Star, my Sun;
And in that Light of life I’ll walk

hymns.title: All my life long I had panted
hymns.author: Clara Tear Williams (1858-1937)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Feeding on the husks around me,
Till my strength was almost gone,
Longed my soul for something better,

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Whom my soul so long has craved!
Through His life I now am saved.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Poor I was, and sought for riches,
But the dust I gathered round me
Only mocked my soul’s sad cry.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Whom my soul so long has craved!
Through His life I now am saved.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Bread of life, so rich and free,

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Whom my soul so long has craved!
Through His life I now am saved.

hymns.title: How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord
hymns.author: "K" in Rippon's Selection of Hymns, 1787

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]How firm a foundation, ye saints of the [Am]Lord,
Is laid for your [C]faith in His [D]excellent [C]word!
What more can He [G]say than to you He hath [Am]said,
To you who for [C]refuge to [D]Jesus have [G]fled?
"Fear not, I am [D]with thee, O [B7]be not dis[Em]mayed,
For I am thy [D]God, and will still give thee [C]aid;
I'll strengthen thee, [G]help thee, and cause thee to [Am]stand,
"When through the deep [D]waters I [B7]call thee to [Em]go,
The rivers of [D]sorrow shall not over[C]flow;
For I will be [G]with thee, thy troubles to [Am]bless,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: “When through fiery trials thy pathway shall lie,
My grace, all sufficient, shall be thy supply;
The flame shall not hurt thee; I only design
Thy dross to consume, and thy gold to refine.”
“E’en down to old age all My people shall prove
And then, when grey hairs shall their temples adorn,
Like lambs they shall still in My bosom be borne.”
“The soul that on Jesus hath leaned for repose,
I will not, I will not desert to his foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,
I’ll never, no, never, no, never forsake!”

hymns.title: There is sunshine in my soul today
hymns.author: Eliza E. Hewitt

When Jesus shows His smiling face

hymns.title: My goal is God Himself
hymns.author: Frances Brook

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]’Tis His to [Bm]lead me there— not [Em7]mine, but [A]His—

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: So faith bounds forward to its goal in God,
And love can trust her Lord to lead her there;
Upheld by Him, my soul is following hard
Till God hath full fulfilled my deepest prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: No matter if the way be sometimes dark,
No matter though the cost be oft-times great,
He knoweth how I best shall reach the mark,
The way that leads to Him must needs be strait.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: One thing I know, I cannot say Him nay;
One thing I do, I press towards my Lord;
My God my glory here, from day to day,
And in the glory there my great Reward.

hymns.title: A common bush
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Just a common bush to be,
Something in which God can dwell,
Something thru which God can speak,
Something thru which God can tell,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Flaming with no light of earth,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Nothing seen but just the flame;
Make me that, just that, O God,
For the glory of Thy Name.

sections.label: Verse 2

sections.label: Verse 3

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou Lord of Life and Light!

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Straight from God’s heart of love;
I break my heart to give Thee room

lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
So shall I think as Thou dost think,
And will as Thou dost will.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
Nor creed, nor form, nor word,
Nor holy Church, nor human love,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
And through this veil of mortal flesh,

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Be Thou supreme, O Jesus Christ,
Nor creed, nor form, nor word,
Nor holy Church, nor human love,

sections.label: Verse 4

hymns.title: Let me love Thee, Thou art claiming
hymns.author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Let me love Thee, come revealing
All Thy love has done for me;
Let me see Thy love despising
All the shame my sins had brought;
What a price my pardon bought.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Let me love Thee, I am gladdest
When I’m loving Thee, the best;
For in sunshine or in sadness
I can find in Thee a rest;
But without Thee life is fading,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Let me love Thee, love is mighty,
Swaying realms of deed and thought;
By it I shall walk uprightly,
I shall serve Thee as I ought:
Love will triumph, love will dare.

hymns.title: Nothing between my soul and the Savior
hymns.author: Charles Albert Tindley (1851-1933)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Habits of life, though harmless they seem,
Must not my heart from Him e’er sever;
He is my all, there’s nothing between.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Nothing between my soul and the Savior,
So that His blessed face may be seen;
Nothing preventing the least of His favor,
Keep the way clear! Let nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Nothing between, like pride or station;
Self-life or friends shall not intervene;
Though it may cost me much tribulation,
I am resolved; there’s nothing between.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Nothing between my soul and the Savior,
So that His blessed face may be seen;
Nothing preventing the least of His favor,
Keep the way clear! Let nothing between.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Nothing between, e’en many hard trials,
Though the whole world against me convene;
Watching with prayer and much self-denial,
I’ll triumph at last, with nothing between.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Nothing between my soul and the Savior,
So that His blessed face may be seen;
Nothing preventing the least of His favor,
Keep the way clear! Let nothing between.

hymns.title: Nothing between, Lord, nothing between
hymns.author: Evan H. Hopkins

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Fading when Thou art near—Nothing between,

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: O’er my whole heart bear sway—Nothing between,

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Thus may I walk with Thee,
Thine only let me be—Nothing between,

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Bursts on my open sight—Nothing between,

hymns.title: Sun of my soul, Thou Savior dear
hymns.author: John Keble (1792-1866)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: When the soft dews of kindly sleep
Be my last thought how sweet to rest

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Abide with me from morn till eve,
For without Thee I cannot live;
Abide with me when night is nigh,
For without Thee I dare not die.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Come near, and bless us when we wake,
Ere through the world our way we take;
Till in the ocean of Thy love
We lose ourselves in Thee above.

hymns.title: If the path I travel
hymns.author: Margaret E. Barber (1869-1930) bio

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: If there’s less of earth joy,
Let the tie that binds us,
Let the tie that binds us,

hymns.title: Savior, lead me up the mountain
hymns.author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Where the strain of effort ceases,
Where in Christ we reign in Life.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Lead me higher up the mountain,
In Thy light I see the fountain,
And the blood it cleanses me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Savior, keep me up the mountain
Till, as one, we share Thine image,
And Thy love and grace extol.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Lead me higher up the mountain,
In Thy light I see the fountain,
And the blood it cleanses me.

hymns.title: Sweet Will of God
hymns.author: Lelia Naylor Morris (1862-1929)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I’m tired of sin, footsore and weary,
The darksome path hath dreary grown,
But now a light has ris’n to cheer me;
I find in Thee my Star, my Sun.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Sweet will of God, still fold me closer,
Till I am wholly lost in Thee;
Sweet will of God, still fold me closer,
Till I am wholly lost in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy precious will, O conqu’ring Savior,
Doth now embrace and compass me;
All discords hushed, my peace a river,
My soul a prisoned bird set free.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Sweet will of God, still fold me closer,
Till I am wholly lost in Thee;
Sweet will of God, still fold me closer,
Till I am wholly lost in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Shut in with Thee, O Lord, forever,
My wayward feet no more to roam;
What pow’r from Thee my soul can sever?
The center of God’s will my home.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Sweet will of God, still fold me closer,
Till I am wholly lost in Thee;
Sweet will of God, still fold me closer,
Till I am wholly lost in Thee.

hymns.title: Lord Jesus, I long in Thy presence to live
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio
themes: For Living in the Lord’s Presence
hymns.subcategory: For Living in the Lord’s Presence

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: From [G]morning to evening my [A7]one world Thou [D7]art;
O let not [G]my heart be con[A]tented or rest

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Each time when I dream of the goodness of life,
I pray Thee, dear Lord, that Thou in it may be;
O do not allow me to choose by myself,
Nor seek any pleasure that’s other than Thee.
Each night when alone in the stillness I lie,
I pray Thee, Lord Jesus, that Thou wilt be near;
Each morning ere dawn comes, while still in my sleep,
Then whispering call me and open my ear.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Each time, Lord, when reading in Thy holy Word,
I pray that Thy glory may shine on each line,
That clearly I’ll see what a Savior I have
And how great salvation that Thou hast made mine.
When helpless I come, Lord, to kneel at Thy throne,
I pray Thee to hear me and grant me Thy grace;
If thru my shortcomings Thou hear not my prayer,
Withdraw not Thy presence, O hide not Thy face.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Each time when of heavenly blessings I think,
O let my heart long to be raptured to Thee;
My only hope here is Thy coming again,
My only joy there, Lord, Thy presence will be.
Lord, teach me each day in Thy presence to live,
From morning to evening my one world Thou art;
O let not my heart be contented or rest
When loving or seeking what with Thee doth part.

hymns.title: Thy way, not mine, O Lord
hymns.author: Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Smooth let it be, or rough,
It will be still the best;

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Thy way, not mine, O Lord,
Lead me by Thine own hand,

hymns.author: Henry Legh Richmond Deck (1853-1910)

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]I take Thy promise, [Dmaj7]Lord, in all its length,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Days may be coming fraught with loss and change,
New scenes surround my life and fancies strange;
I thank Thee that no day can ever break,
Savior, when Thou wilt leave me or forsake.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: There may be days of darkness and distress,
When sin has power to tempt, and care to press,
Yet in the darkest day I will not fear,
For, ’mid the shadows, Thou wilt still be near.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Days there may be of joy and deep delight,
When earth seems fairest, and her skies most bright,
Then draw me closer to Thee, lest I rest
Elsewhere, my Savior, than upon Thy breast.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: And all the other days that make my life,
Marked by no special joy or grief or strife,
Days filled with quiet duties, trivial care,
Burdens too small for other hearts to share;

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Spend Thou these days with me, all shall be Thine,
So shall the darkest hour with glory shine.
Then when these earthly years have passed away,
Let me be with Thee in the perfect day.

hymns.title: My will is weak, my strength is frail
hymns.author: Watchman Nee (1903-1972) bio

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [G]My will is weak, [Bm]my strength is frail,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: I’ve tried my best, but still have failed,
E’en as before I’ve failed and erred;
Thy patience is my only trust
To hold and keep me to Thy word.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Whene’er my heart is lifted up,
How very near I am to fall;
I dare not do, I dare not think,
I need Thyself in great or small.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou art my Savior, strength and stay,
O Lord, I come to seek Thy face;
Though I’m the weakest of the weak,
My strength is nothing but Thy grace.

hymns.title: Lord, I was blind; I could not see
hymns.author: William Tidd Matson (1833-1899)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, I was deaf; I could not hear
The thrilling music of Thy voice;
But now I hear Thee and rejoice,
And all Thine uttered words are dear!

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, I was dumb; I could not speak
The grace and glory of Thy name;
But now, as touched with living flame,
My lips Thine eager praises wake.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord, I was dead; I could not stir
My lifeless soul to come to Thee;
But now, since Thou hast quickened me,
I rise from sin’s dark sepulcher.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: For Thou hast made the blind to see,
The deaf to hear, the dumb to speak,
The dead to live; and, lo, I break

hymns.title: My God, my Portion
hymns.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: To Thee I owe my wealth, and friends,
Thanks to Thy name for meaner things,
But they are not my God.
How vain a toy is glittering wealth,
Or what’s my safety, or my health,
Or all my friends to me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Were I possessor of the earth,
And called the stars my own,
Let others stretch their arms like seas,
And grasp in all the shore;
Grant me the visits of Thy grace,

hymns.title: My home is God Himself
hymns.author: Frances Brook, adapted

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]My home is God Himself; Christ [G]brought me there,
And [A]bade me dwell in Him, re[D]joicing there;
He [G]bore me [A7]where no foot but [F♯m]His hath [Bm]trod,

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: A long, long road I traveled night and day,
And sought to find within myself some way,
Aught I could do, or feel to bring me near;
Self effort failed, and I was filled with fear,
And then I found Christ was the only way
That I must come to Him and in Him stay.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: O wondrous place! O home divinely fair!
And I, God’s little one, safe hidden there.
Lord, as I dwell in Thee and Thou in me,
So make me dead to everything but Thee;
That as I rest within my home most fair,
I’ll share my God in all and everywhere.

hymns.title: Art thou hung’ring for the fulness
hymns.author: F. H. Allen

lines: O’er the life He died to win,
Shall His Spirit work through thee,
While thy soul this witness beareth,
’Tis not I, but Christ in me.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: In Him dwelleth all God’s fulness,
In Him thou art made complete;
Rise, and claim thy heavenly birthright,
Praise Him that the gift is thine;
Then go forth to live each moment

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord, I come, and simply resting
I believe the blood doth cleanse me,
And that Christ is crowned Lord.
Of Thy life and love through me;
Reaching those who sit in darkness,

hymns.title: Within the veil
hymns.author: F. H. Allen; R. B.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: [D]"Within the Veil": be this, belov'd, thy [Em]portion,
Thy [A]life His love, thy [E7]lips His praise shall [A]tell.

lines: “Within the Veil,” for only as thou gazest
Upon the matchless beauty of His face,
Canst thou become a living revelation
Of His great heart of love, His untold grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: “Within the Veil,” His fragrance poured upon thee,
Without the Veil, that fragrance shed abroad;
“Within the Veil,” His hand shall tune the music
Which sounds on earth the praises of Thy Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: “Within the Veil,” thy spirit deeply anchored,
Thou walkest calm above a world of strife;
“Within the Veil,” thy soul with Him united,

hymns.title: Take time to behold Him

hymns.title: Trust Him when thy wants are many
hymns.author: Lucy A. Bennett

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Trust Him when thy soul is burdened
With the sense of all its sin;
He will speak the word of pardon,
He will make thee clean within.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Trust Him for the grace sufficient,
Trust Him always for the answer,
When in His dear name you plead.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: Trust Him for the grace to conquer,
Trust Him for the power for service;
Trust Him for the blessing too.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: Trust Him when dark doubts assail thee,
Trust Him when thy strength is small,
Trust Him when to simply trust Him
Seems the hardest thing of all.

sections.label: Verse 6
lines: Trust Him; He is ever faithful;
Trust Him, for His will is best;
Trust Him, for the heart of Jesus
Is the only place of rest.

sections.label: Verse 7
lines: Trust Him, then, through cloud or sunshine,
All thy cares upon Him cast,
Till the storm of life is over,
And the trusting days are past.

Thy will is mine, whate’er it be.

lines: When tender joys to me are known,

I know my cup is filled by Thee;
Thy will is mine, whate’er it be.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Whate’er it be! whate’er it be!
I do not fear, whate’er it be!
Thy will is mine, whate’er it be.

lines: Thus calmly do I face my lot,

Thy will is mine, whate’er it be.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Whate’er it be! whate’er it be!

Thy will is mine, whate’er it be.

And every hour in perfect peace,

hymns.title: Begone, unbelief
hymns.author: John Newton

hymns.title: God Hath Not Promised (1)
hymns.author: Annie Johnson Flint (1866-1932)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: God hath not promised we shall not know
Toil and temptation, trouble and woe;
He hath not told us we shall not bear
Many a burden, many a care.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: But God hath promised strength for the day,
Rest for the labor, light for the way,
Grace for the trials, help from above,

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: God hath not promised smooth roads and wide,
Swift, easy travel, needing no guide;
Never a mountain, rocky and steep,

sections.label: Chorus 3

hymns.title: I’ll sing of the wonderful promise
hymns.author: Albert Benjamin Simpson (1843-1919)

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: His grace is sufficient to save me,
And cleanse me from guilt and from sin;
And give me His Spirit within.
His grace is sufficient for trials,
No matter how hard they may be,
This promise stands over against them,
My grace is sufficient for thee.

sections.label: Chorus 2
lines: Yes, over and over and over,
My Savior keeps saying to me;
My strength is made perfect in weakness,
My grace is sufficient for thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: His grace is sufficient for sickness,
His grace is sufficient when sorrows
Like billows roll over the soul.
His grace is sufficient for service,
It sets us from selfishness free,
And sends us to tell to the tried ones,
His grace is sufficient for thee.

sections.label: Chorus 3
lines: Yes, over and over and over,
My Savior keeps saying to me;
My strength is made perfect in weakness,
My grace is sufficient for thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
lines: His grace is sufficient to live by,
And should we be summoned to die
’Twill light up the valley of shadows,
And bear us away to Him nigh.
Or when we shall stand in His vict’ry,
And Christ in His glory shall see,
We’ll fall at His footstool confessing,
Thy grace was sufficient for me.

sections.label: Chorus 4
lines: Yes, over and over and over,
My Savior keeps saying to me;
My strength is made perfect in weakness,
My grace is sufficient for thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
lines: It is not our grace that’s sufficient,
But His grace, it ever must be:
Our graces are transient and changing;
His grace is unfailing as He.
And so I am ever repeating
My strength is made perfect in weakness,
My grace is sufficient for thee.

sections.label: Chorus 5
lines: Yes, over and over and over,
My Savior keeps saying to me;

My grace is sufficient for thee.
